title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform—the partitioned-acs (pacs) net—has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D2h ligands with lower-symmetry C2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned-acs), with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2)1/3. The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C2H2/CO2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg−1 vs 0.98 mol kg−1).

title: Western Pacific double subduction drives Gulf of California rifting
abstract: Continental rifting reflects the balance between tectonic forces and lithospheric strength, yet the mechanisms of breakup remain debated. Rapid rifting of the Gulf of California oblique rift (GOCOR) ~6 million to 8 million years ago is a key example; it may have resulted from the lithosphere responding to external kinematics or acceleration of long-lived extension. The dynamics of either scenario remain incompletely understood. In this study, we highlight that the rapid rifting of the GOCOR coincides with the initiation of Western Pacific double subduction. Using three-dimensional geodynamic models, we show that such subduction reorganization can transmit extensional stresses of ~5 to 15 megapascals across the Pacific plate, loading the GOCOR and the southern San Andreas fault. Subduction reorganization may represent the missing driver for the initiation of rapid GOCOR rifting within a preconditioned lithosphere and may be an overlooked tectonic force behind other rifting events.

title: Retarding efficiency loss upon scaling in perovskite photovoltaics as fill factor becomes the bottleneck
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Perovskite solar cells approach crystalline-silicon efficiencies at small areas, yet substantial performance losses during scale-up hinder their translation into practical modules. Here we quantify the contributions of device-performance parameters to efficiency loss during scale-up across diverse perovskite technologies, identifying fill factor (FF" role="presentation">FF{FF}) as a major contributor and target for mitigating this loss. Further analysis resolves the FF deficit into voltage-, diode-non-ideality- and transport-associated contributions. Cryo-controlled processing provides an experimental route to preserve FF" role="presentation">FF{FF} by regulating intermediate-phase evolution during crystallization. The resulting FF" role="presentation">FF{FF}-preservation advantage arises predominantly from reduced diode non-ideality, with the other contributions being smaller. This advantage increases across device scales. A mini-module (19.48 cm2 aperture) achieves a record certified steady-state efficiency of 23.9% with an FF" role="presentation">FF{FF} of 83.3%, the highest reported for perovskite modules. The same FF" role="presentation">FF{FF} limitation governs operational performance decay, linking efficiency retention during scale-up with long-term stability. Together, these results establish FF" role="presentation">FF{FF} preservation and the factors governing it as central to mitigating performance loss during scale-up and operation.

title: Tribovoltaic Effect-Driven Contact-Electro-Catalysis at a MoS2–Water Interface
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Contact-electro-catalysis (CEC) enables mechanically driven interfacial redox reactions through contact-induced charge transfer. Most CEC systems rely on dielectric or insulating materials, whereas the role of semiconductor carrier dynamics remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a tribovoltaic effect-driven CEC mechanism at a MoS2–water solid–liquid interface, where mechanical contact dynamically modulates semiconductor carriers and interfacial electron transfer. Electrical measurements and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal that contact electrification and tribovoltaic carrier modulation synergistically regulate the interfacial electronic state. This coupled charge-transfer process promotes oxygen reduction to H2O2, which is subsequently activated to generate highly reactive •OH. Notably, under identical experimental conditions, the MoS2-based tribovoltaic-CEC system exhibits approximately 88-fold higher •OH production from H2O2 than conventional FEP- and PVDF-based CEC systems. Radical trapping, theoretical calculations and in situ fluorescence imaging further establish the relationship between interfacial charge transfer, oxygen activation and reactive oxygen species generation. Under ultrasound-assisted conditions, the system achieves approximately 90% degradation of tetracycline and efficient bacterial disinfection in real lake water. Our findings reveal the tribovoltaic effect as a potential mechanistic contributor to semiconductor catalytic activity, offering a new perspective on and a potential strategy for dynamically tuning solid–liquid interfacial catalysis through mechanically regulated carrier transfer.

title: Ultrasound-Driven Lysis of Tumor-Resident Bacteria Awakens Innate Immunity for Systemic Cancer Therapy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tumor-resident bacteria establish a profound immunosuppressive microenvironment that compromises cancer immunotherapy. While ablating these microbes holds therapeutic promise, broad-spectrum antibiotics can cause systemic dysbiosis, and the Gram-negative outer membrane can restrict the entry of conventional sonosensitizers, limiting the antibacterial efficacy of sonodynamic therapy (SDT). Here, we report an ultrasound-driven, bacteria-targeted immunotherapy utilizing polyarginine-functionalized peptide-sonosensitizer conjugates to achieve the in situ pulverization of the tumor Fusobacterium nucleatum (F. nucleatum), thereby eliciting potent innate antitumor immunity. The cationic conjugates electrostatically intercalate into Gram-negative bacterial membranes, inflicting a structural predisruption. Subsequent ultrasound irradiation synergizes localized sonochemical oxidation with mechanical shear forces to thoroughly shatter the bacteria. This targeted microbial fragmentation liberates massive quantities of pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) that, unlike tumor-derived signals from conventional SDT, decisively reprogram macrophages toward an antitumor M1 phenotype to awaken innate immunity. Synchronized with tumor-specific antigens released via conjugate-induced immunogenic cell death, the liberated PAMPs synergistically amplify antigen presentation and optimally drive dendritic cell maturation. In a bacteria-colonized murine colorectal cancer model, this localized therapy markedly suppressed primary tumor growth and elicited both a pronounced abscopal effect against distant tumors and antitumor immune memory. By repurposing complicit bacteria into potent endogenous adjuvants, this ultrasound-driven strategy reverses bacteria-mediated immunosuppression, offering a transformative paradigm for treating microbiome-colonized solid tumors.

title: Not Every Semicircle Is Interfacial: High-Frequency Shielding Artifacts in Three-Electrode Electrochemical Impedance Measurements
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is widely used to investigate interfacial processes and transport properties of electrochemical systems. Three-electrode configurations are commonly employed to separate the impedance contributions from individual electrodes; however, the influence of reference electrode structures on high-frequency impedance measurements has received limited attention. In this work, we identify a high-frequency artifact in three-electrode EIS measurements caused by the insulating sheath of the conventional reference electrodes. Using Ag/Ag2O reference electrodes as a model system, an additional high-frequency semicircle was observed in the impedance spectra. Through systematic experiments, this feature is shown to be independent of the electrode materials, electrolyte composition, and instrumental parasitic capacitance. Finite-element simulations further demonstrate that the dielectric sheath around the reference electrode disturbs the local alternating electric-field distribution, resulting in an artificial relaxation process associated with dielectric shielding. The intensity of this artifact depends on the reference electrode geometry and electrolyte dielectric properties, and the same phenomenon is observed in both the aqueous and organic electrolytes. These results indicate that accurate three-electrode EIS measurements require not only sufficient ionic contact between the reference electrode and electrolyte but also minimal disturbance of the local electric-field distribution.

title: Elucidation of the Azotobacter vinelandii FixABCX Energy Landscape Reveals a Conformationally Gated Flavin-Based Electron Bifurcation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electron bifurcation was first used to describe the electron-transfer events associated with the quinone-cycle (Q-cycle), which occurs in complex III of the electron transport chain. Decades later, flavin-based electron bifurcation (FBEB) was discovered, where flavin cofactors act in analogy to Q to drive the endergonic reduction of ferredoxin (Fd) or flavodoxin (Fld) by NAD(P)H. The soil microbeAzotobacter vinelandii is known to generate low-potential electrons in the form of reduced Fd or Fld using FBEB via the enzyme complex FixABCX. FixABCX in A. vinelandii (AvFixABCX) couples the exergonic reduction of coenzyme Q (E = +10 mV) to the endergonic reduction of Fd/Fld (E = ∼−450 mV) during NADH oxidation (E = −320 mV). In this work, we successfully optimized the expression of AvFixABCX in E. coli. We have employed protein thin-film electrochemistry, UV–vis spectrophotometry, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy, and transient absorption (TA) spectroscopy to elucidate the complete energy landscape, and structural characterization methods, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), and cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) to show the dynamics of the complex energy landscape during AvFixABCX electron-transfer catalysis. Our results show that AvFixABCX contains two [4Fe-4S] clusters with disparate reduction potentials: the higher-potential cluster participates in the exergonic electron-transfer pathway, whereas the lower-potential cluster is off-pathway. We experimentally determined that AvFixABCX undergoes a conformationally gated, reversible FBEB mechanism to simultaneously reduce coenzyme Q and the semiquinone state of Fld during NADH oxidation.

title: Layer-wise Prediction for Interpretation of Hidden Representations in Deep Neural Networks through Evolving Probability Distributions
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The sequential architecture of DNNs enables accurate predictions by encoding input features, yet their limited interpretability and transparency during forward propagation undermine the credibility of predictions. Therefore, we propose layer-wise prediction for interpretation method (LPI), which involves mapping the representation from each layer to a probability distribution, explaining the hidden-layer prediction process. To ensure interpretation fidelity to DNN mechanisms, we employ a reconstruction strategy to map probability distributions back to hidden layer features while reducing their influence on model prediction. Meanwhile, we define a rank-index metric to quantify the consistency of probability distribution evolution. Furthermore, we show how each hidden layer probability distribution evolves consistently during DNN forward propagation. Experiments on various models show that LPI achieves superior performance in consistency, stability, fidelity and certainty, outperforming AdditionalLayer, SDN, MetaGF, and DFS. Notably, LPI not only enhances deep learning interpretability but also provides valuable insights into reliable and credible model security assessment.

title: Establishing Oxime as a Bioresponsive Group on Naphthalene Diimide: Visual Bacterial Classification and NIR-II Photothermal Antibacterial
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bioresponsive groups are fundamental tools in engineering activatable constructs. Herein, we first demonstrated that the oxime group was a bioresponsive group by designing oxime-naphthalene diimide (NONDI). The oxime group could be reduced to an iminyl group by bacteria, and NONDI was completely converted into iminyl-naphthalene diimide (NHNDI). Mechanistically, that reduction triggered homolytic cleavage of the N–O bond in the oxime group and released a hydroxyl radical. NONDI could be reduced stepwise to NHNDI, NHNDI•–, and NHNDI2–, yielding four distinct colors which depended on the bacteria with reducibility from weak to strong. In other words, NONDI enables visual classification of bacteria by their reducing ability. In addition, the intense NIR-II absorption of NHNDI•– endows it with photothermal antibacterial properties. This work uncovers fundamental principles of oxime bioresponsiveness under reducing conditions for the first time, providing a new platform for designing new activatable materials.

title: Interfacially Stitched Bilayer Anodes Enforce Surface-Confined Hydroxyl Radical Chemistry in Complex Wastewater
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electro-oxidation technology holds great promise for wastewater treatment, yet its practical application remains hindered by insufficient selectivity in oxidative species generation and limited electrode stability under harsh operating conditions. Here, we devise a layer-by-layer anion–cation engineering strategy to fabricate an Sb–F-stitched SnO2 bilayer anode (SF–SnO2 BA), in which a fluorine-regulated SnO2 catalytic layer is interfacially anchored onto a dense Sb–SnO2 interlayer coated on a Ti foam scaffold. This hierarchically stitched architecture simultaneously modulates interfacial charge transport and stabilizes the catalytic layer, leading to markedly enhanced electrocatalytic oxidation performance across a broad pH range (1–11). When integrated into a scalable flow-through electro-oxidation system, SF–SnO2 BA enabled highly efficient mineralization (>80%) of four representative industrial wastewaters at low energy consumption. Furthermore, the system also demonstrated remarkable operational durability, sustaining high mineralization efficiency (60–80%) over 14 consecutive days during continuous treatment of real aniline wastewater from a coal chemical plant. In situ spectroscopic investigations coupled with theoretical calculations collectively elucidated that water molecules are initially oxidized on the SF–SnO2 BA surface to form Sn–OH intermediates, which are subsequently transformed into Sn–O species at elevated potentials. Notably, the cooperative F···Sn–O* structural motif directs the generation of surface-confined •OH, which acts as the dominant oxidative species for pollutant degradation. This interfacially stitched bilayer anode offers a viable route toward green and sustainable electrochemical oxidation technologies for practical wastewater treatment.

title: An Air- and Moisture-Stable Fulvalene Radical Cation in a Reversible Three-State Redox Interconversion
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pentafulvalene has attracted considerable interest owing to its unique cross-conjugated electronic structure, but its intrinsic instability has limited detailed studies of its redox chemistry, particularly with respect to accessing and characterizing its radical form. Herein, we report an imidazolium-substituted zwitterionic fulvalene (IZFv) that undergoes reversible interconversion among three isolable redox states, including a fulvalene radical cation. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction, spectroscopy, and complementary NICS, HOMA, and AICD analyses reveal systematic oxidation-state-dependent changes in the structure and local aromaticity of the fulvalene framework. Notably, the dication (IZFv2+) shows the closest bond-metric and aromaticity correspondence to parent pentafulvalene (Fv) while remaining isolable and amenable to handling under ambient conditions. The radical cation (IZFv•+) is stable toward air and moisture (t1/2 = 15.2 days), exhibits a distonic electronic structure in which the unpaired spin resides predominantly on the fulvalene core while the positive charge is accommodated primarily by the imidazolium-derived carbon centers, and shows red photoluminescence at 650 nm. To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first isolation of an oxidatively generated radical cation based on a sulfur-free, unannulated pentafulvalene scaffold and establishes an experimentally accessible platform for examining redox-dependent structural and electronic evolution within the fulvalene π-framework.

title: Chemically Engineered Carbon Nanotubes Map Class-Selective Metabolite Enrichment from Human Plasma
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The spontaneous adsorption of biomolecules onto nanoparticle surfaces has been extensively characterized at the protein level, but the metabolite corona remains poorly defined, in part because low annotation rates inherent to untargeted metabolomics limit systematic, class-level analysis. To address this analytical challenge, we developed a multimodal liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry workflow combined with machine-learning classifiers, extending metabolite class annotations from 10 to 45% coverage to the full detected set and enabling the first class-level mapping of metabolite corona composition across 25 chemically modified carbon nanotubes in human plasma. Complementary analytical conditions detected approximately 9,000 metabolite features, of which over 5,000 yielded valid corona-versus-plasma enrichment measurements. We find that polymer wrapping dominates corona composition, and covalent quantum well defects further modulate class-level enrichment in a structure- and chemistry-dependent manner. Our findings demonstrate that chemically modified carbon nanotubes can serve as tunable, selective scaffolds for metabolite enrichment, potentially enhancing the capability to recruit and detect structurally diverse, low-abundance small molecules in complex biofluids.

title: Programming MOF Topology through Twelve-Connected Linker Isomerism
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Linker isomerism represents a powerful, yet unexploited, strategy for programming framework topology and unlocking chemical complexity in high-connectivity reticular systems. Here, we demonstrate the reticular synthesis of two 12-connected nanographene-based zirconium metal–organic frameworks, MOF-1300 and MOF-1400, wherein network architecture is directed by the meta versus para carboxylate substitution patterns of a 12-connected linker, dodeca-carboxylate hexakis[3,5-bis(m/p-carboxyphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]hexabenzocoronene (m/p-HBC-LH12). The meta isomer directs the assembly of an 8-connected cubic Zr cluster to yield MOF-1300 with an unprecedented trinodal (3,6,8)-c rcb1 net, representing a new topology in reticular chemistry. Conversely, the para isomer enforces 12-connectivity at the Zr cluster with hexagonal prismatic geometry to yield MOF-1400 with a rare trinodal (3,6,12)-c kex net which has not previously been observed in Zr-MOFs. Beyond structure, both frameworks serve as solid reservoirs of photoactive nanographenes: under basic photoredox conditions, they release their molecular HBC linkers, which act as homogeneous organophotoredox catalysts for the hydrodefluorination of polyfluoroarenes under simulated solar light (AM 1.5G). This behavior highlights the potential of reticular materials as precatalysts for the delivery of molecular photocatalysts and provides a basis for exploring such materials in future photocatalytic applications.

title: Viral tRNA-like structure hijacks host ribosomes for poly(A)-independent translation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Positive-sense RNA viruses often use 3′ tRNA-like structures (TLSs) instead of poly(A) tails to capture the host translation machinery. While TLSs resemble canonical tRNAs and engage host factors, their ability to directly recruit ribosomes has remained unresolved. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy snapshots of the histidine-accepting TLS (TLSHis) from tobacco mosaic virus bound to the tobacco 60S subunit, the 80S ribosome, and the 80S-tRNAiMet initiation complex. Across these states, TLSHis is consistently anchored to the L1 stalk of 60S, even under cycloheximide treatment, yet remains dynamic on the 40S subunit. Structural analysis shows that TLSHis transitions from the E-site to an adjacent Z-site to accommodate initiator tRNA. Functional assays show that TLSHis preferentially associates with ribosomal subunits over polysomes and can substitute for a poly(A) tail to promote robust cap-dependent translation. These results provide structural and mechanistic evidence that the viral tRNA mimic exploits the tRNA-exit channel to stabilize initiation-competent ribosomes and drive poly(A)-independent translation.

title: Stabilization of insulin receptor mRNA by Star-PAP in metabolic homeostasis
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Conserved polyadenylation b3y poly(A) polymerases (PAPs) is essential for mRNA stability, yet its metabolic functions remain unclear. Here we identify a rare variant p.D469N (Asp469Asn) in Star-PAP present in lean individuals but absent in obese cases. Adipose-specific Star-PAP knockout mice develop progressive adipose tissue loss, hepatic steatosis, and severe insulin resistance, phenocopying human lipodystrophy. Mechanistically, Star-PAP directly binds the insulin receptor (InsR) mRNA 3’–UTR to stabilize its transcript. Both deletion of Star-PAP and p.D469N variant decrease InsR mRNA maturation. Star-PAP deficiency impairs insulin receptor signaling and adipocyte lipid storage, while restoring InsR in adipocytes partially ameliorates the lipodystrophic phenotypes. Notably, Star-PAP deficiency disrupts acetyl-CoA homeostasis secondary to insulin signaling defects, accompanied by reduced histone acetylation at fatty acid synthesis genes. Pyruvate supplementation effectively restores acetyl-CoA levels and histone acetylation, thereby rescuing the gene expression and lipogenesis. Together, our results identify Star-PAP-mediated RNA polyadenylation as a mechanism governing adipose mass, positioning Star-PAP as a key regulator of insulin receptor signaling and lipodystrophy.

title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus. Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus. Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus.

title: Aberrant thymic architecture and enhanced interferon signaling in Down syndrome
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) have an elevated risk of autoimmune disease, particularly celiac disease, type 1 diabetes, and autoimmune hypothyroidism. In DS, thymi show characteristic structural and cellular changes, but the connection between these and the propensity to autoimmune disease is still unclear. Here we present a cell atlas from single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics of age-matched thymi from infants with and without DS, which might contribute to filling this knowledge gap. DS does not significantly alter CD34+ diversity in the thymus; however, the gene expression changes we observe indicate altered differentiative potential in DS CD34+ cells. Although many genes involved in T-cell development and function (including USP16, RUNX1 and ETS2) are located on chromosome 21, several important T cell regulatory genes that are located on other chromosomes also change in DS. In contrast, CD34- DS thymocytes are characterised by maturation defects. CD34+ progenitors and proliferating DP thymocytes are in a functional state of chronic interferon activation. In summary, we identify several notable differences in key functional cellular subsets and pathways within the DS thymus, providing insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of the thymic environment for this genetic condition.

title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
abstract:
Abstract
                  Most disaster risk assessments use asset damages as their central metric, often neglecting distributional impacts and affected people’s coping and recovery capacity. To address this, the concepts of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience—the ability to experience asset damages without a decline in well-being—have been proposed. Here we provide a global picture of well-being losses and socio-economic resilience using microsimulations. Across 132 countries, 1 dollar in damages causes well-being losses equivalent to a 2-dollar uniform national consumption drop. The poorest populations incur only 9% of damages but 33% of well-being losses. A 10% higher gross domestic product per capita is associated with a 1 percentage point resilience increase. Low-income countries experience 72% greater well-being losses per dollar of damages and need 92% longer to recover than high-income countries. Socio-economic and financial interventions can complement asset-focused policies, and targeting low-income populations usually yields higher well-being returns. Our results offer a starting point for a discussion on more comprehensive risk metrics and risk management policies for sustainable development.

title: Dynamically and Reversibly Functionalized Self-Assembled Platelets via Noncovalent Interactions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The creation of polymeric assemblies with reconfigurable surface functionality remains a major challenge for programmable soft materials. Covalent modification strategies can provide stable functional materials, but often require harsh reaction conditions or irreversible bond formation. Here, we integrate noncovalent interactions with crystallization-driven self-assembly (CDSA) to construct polymer platelets with region-selective functionalization and controllable responsiveness under mild conditions. Polycaprolactone-based platelets bearing cyclodextrin, barbituric acid, or related recognition motifs were prepared and subsequently orthogonal modified with complementary fluorescent guests through host–guest interactions or hydrogen bonding. Confocal fluorescence microscopy confirmed platelet-localized dye incorporation, while competitive displacement and relabeling demonstrated reversible molecular loading and release without disrupting platelet structural integrity. This work establishes supramolecular modification of CDSA-based assemblies as a modular route to soft materials with controllable and reconfigurable molecular functionality under mild conditions.

title: On living and feeling better
abstract: As the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) enter their final years, there is a desire to reflect on their societal impact. A study now compares changes in the SDG indicators with changes in how people feel about their lives and finds no detectable correlation between the two.

title: Cooperative Photocarrier Utilization Enables Dual-Channel Alcohol Dehydrogenation for Benzimidazole Synthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic oxidative dehydrogenative coupling of alcohols and o-phenylenediamines offers a sustainable route to benzimidazole, yet conventional systems suffer from severe charge recombination and largely underutilized photogenerated electrons, limited to single-channel hole activation. Herein, we report gold-nanoparticle-decorated hafnium metal–organic layers (Au/Hf-MOL), which achieve efficient utilization of photogenerated charge carriers via an aerobic dual-channel mechanism. Upon light irradiation, effective separation of photogenerated electrons and holes takes place over Au/Hf-MOL. The photogenerated electrons migrate onto the surface of Au nanoparticles (Au NPs) and activate molecular oxygen (O2) into superoxide radicals. These two reactive species, namely superoxide radicals and photogenerated holes, work cooperatively to realize dual activation of the α-C–H bonds in alcohol molecules. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the anchored Au NPs not only boost spatial charge-carrier separation, but also facilitate the coadsorption of O2 and alcohol substrates. Consequently, the reaction energy barriers for oxygen activation and ethanol dehydrogenation are reduced. The optimized catalyst delivers an unprecedented benzimidazole (MBZ) formation rate of 10 mmol g–1 h–1 with 100% selectivity, outperforming state-of-the-art photocatalysts. In situ spectroscopy, radical tests and Density functional theory (DFT) calculations verify the synergistic dual-redox pathway. Furthermore, the catalyst exhibits robust cycling stability and broad substrate tolerance. This work establishes an O2-mediated dual-channel strategy to maximize photocarrier efficiency, offering a promising paradigm for high-value alcohol upgrading.

title: Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF 2
abstract: Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF 2 showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF 2 . This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.

title: Even stupendous black holes can’t explain dark matter
abstract: The theoretical objects would have left a larger imprint on cosmic radiation if they were a source of the invisible force pulling together the galaxies.

title: AI is shaking up math. But can its proofs be trusted?
abstract: As AI companies churn out math breakthroughs, their proofchecking system comes under scrutiny

title: Global arable land redistribution toward the tropics and drylands under human settlement expansion
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Arable land extent has undergone widespread changes across many regions worldwide through processes such as urban encroachment, forest conversion to agriculture, and dryland farming expansion. Yet an integrated understanding of global arable land dynamics remains limited. Using our self-developed arable land product integrated with global human settlement layers, Köppen–Geiger climate classifications, and historical land-use reconstructions, we show that the disproportionate climatic co-location of arable land and human settlements fundamentally structures global arable land dynamics. Across much of the climatically favorable Northern Hemisphere, earlier co-development of settlements and agriculture has increasingly shifted toward competition, with settlement expansion displacing cultivation from temperate regions and contributing to its expansion into adjacent arid zones. In contrast, low-latitude tropical regions continue to expand both systems at the expense of natural landscapes, partly driven by agricultural investment from Northern Hemisphere. Globally, these contrasting trajectories reveal a broader redistribution of agricultural pressure from climatically favorable regions toward less-exploited tropical and arid environments, linking settlement expansion and agricultural displacement to diverse environmental consequences including deforestation, biodiversity loss, groundwater depletion, and vegetation greening. These findings highlight the need to consider both local settlement–agriculture competition and broader agricultural redistribution when planning future food production and settlement growth.

title: Glacial CO2 drawdown by plankton metabolic balance
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Which mechanisms caused the Holocene-versus-Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) difference? This longstanding question is crucial for characterizing glacial-interglacial cycles and using LGM climate information in climate predictions. We argue that the metabolic temperature dependence of epipelagic plankton is an important mechanism. Autotrophic plankton metabolisms are less sensitive to temperature than heterotrophic ones. Colder waters can thereby export and thus sequester more carbon in the deep ocean. We develop a theoretical model from Metabolic Theory of Ecology principles, then validate its predictions with empirical data compilations. We then use temperature reconstructions to estimate the plankton metabolism-driven LGM CO2 anomaly. Holding all other conditions at their pre-industrial state, such as net primary production and buffering capacity, we find that this mechanism represents a 6.2 ± 0.9ppm per degree global mean sea surface temperature change feedback, and can potentially explain 20 ± 5ppm, or ~ 1/4 of the total ~ 90ppm LGM CO2 anomaly. We diagnose a similar 18ppm using model data from an intermediate complexity Earth System Model that considers glacial-interglacial differences in nutrient limitation and primary production. Our findings are consistent with several temperature-driven mechanisms acting concertedly to modulate glacial-interglacial CO2 variations.

title: Taking the brakes off a stress response
abstract: A small molecule improves the fitness of cells containing diseased mitochondria

title: Emergence of Chern metal in a moiré Kondo lattice
abstract: A Chern metal is a two-dimensional metallic state of matter carrying chiral edge states. We report the observation of a Chern metal at the onset of the magnetic Kondo breakdown in a frustrated moiré Kondo lattice--angle-aligned MoTe 2 /WSe 2 bilayers. The state is compressible and is manifested by a nearly quantized Hall resistance and a finite longitudinal resistance arising from a bad metallic bulk. We demonstrate the presence of a chiral edge state by nonlocal transport measurements and current-induced quantum anomalous Hall breakdown. Magnetic circular dichroism measurements further reveal a magnetization plateau for the Chern metal before a metamagnetic transition at the Kondo breakdown. Our results open an opportunity for moiré engineering of exotic quantum phases through the interplay between band topology and Kondo interactions.

title: Spatial coordination in the codevelopment of the human urogenital system during organogenesis
abstract: The human urogenital system originates from a common embryonic domain, yet the mechanisms guiding its spatiotemporal coordination remain understudied. Here, we combined high-resolution spatial transcriptomics with single-cell multiomics to profile human embryos from Carnegie stages 15 to 23, capturing the codevelopmental dynamics of the urogenital system. We revealed mesonephros- and adrenal primordium–derived signals that promote gonadal specification and enable efficient in vitro generation of cells resembling early gonadal lineages. We also uncovered a possible mesonephric origin of gonadal supporting cells through rete testis or ovarii linking the mesonephros. Finally, we delineate three transcriptionally distinct steroidogenic lineages differing in cholesterol sourcing, cortisol synthesis, and sex hormone production that together orchestrate sex differentiation. These findings deepen our understanding of urogenital system assembly and guide the exploration of coordinated multiorgan development.

title: A wireless magnetic implant system for continuous neuromuscular sensing
abstract: A skin-mounted magnetometer array that wirelessly tracks implanted magnetic beads enables precise neuromuscular sensing and neuroprosthetic control that match or exceed those achievable with electromyography.

title: Wearable sensing of muscle dynamics towards anthropometric control
abstract: A wearable and wireless platform enables real-time simultaneous tracking of magnetic beads implanted in muscle, thus providing high-fidelity biomimetic neuroprosthetic control in people with transtibial amputation.

title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
abstract: Two-dimensional metal oxides offer a versatile platform for exploring quantum phenomena and enable functionalities beyond those of their bulk counterparts. Despite advances in synthesizing ultrathin and free-standing oxides, controlled fabrication at the single-atomic-layer limit has remained a formidable challenge. Here we report the controlled fabrication of diverse free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides (MO), including CrO, ErO and BiO, down to the single-atomic-layer limit via electron-beam-induced dehalogenation of layered metal oxyhalides (MOX). Using monolayer CrO as a representative system, which features a single-atomic-layer square lattice, we obtain free-standing single-crystalline domains exceeding 104 nm2 and demonstrate controllable patterning at the micrometre scale. Density functional theory confirms both the thermodynamic and kinetic stability of free-standing monolayer CrO, predicting a Néel antiferromagnetic order below 230 K. Combined experimental and theoretical analysis reveals that ionization-driven halogen selective removal and lattice relaxation underpin the CrOCl-to-CrO transformation, a conversion mechanism potentially extendable to other metal oxyhalides. This approach further enables the fabrication of MOX-MO lateral heterostructures as well as aligned and twisted metal oxide bilayers, which exhibit pronounced excitonic responses with an unusually large exciton binding energy. Our work opens opportunities for two-dimensional metal oxide monolayers, heterostructures and moiré superlattices, and for exploring emergent excitonic phenomena in low-dimensional oxides.

title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Anisotropic van der Waals materials exhibit direction-dependent optical and electronic properties, enabling tailored directional light–matter interactions. Rhenium disulfide (ReS
                    2
                    ) stands out among them for its strong in-plane anisotropy and thickness-independent direct-bandgap excitons. These excitons can hybridize with light to form exciton–polaritons, rendering ReS
                    2
                    a compelling material for nanophotonic integration. Metasurfaces are arrays of subwavelength resonators and can support ultrasharp quasi-bound states in the continuum resonances. Topological transformations of their band structure can give rise to flatbands, which host dispersionless states with quenched kinetic energy and vanishing group velocity. Here we show that structuring ReS
                    2
                    into a resonant metasurface reshapes its photonic band topology, splitting the integer topological charge of the quasi-bound states in the continuum into two half-integer polarization singularities and driving the formation of directional far-field flatbands. Tuned into resonance with the linearly polarized excitonic transitions of ReS
                    2
                    , these flatband states hybridize into distinct directionally polarized exciton–polaritons. This points towards a scalable route to polarization-resolved quantum emitters, flatband-enhanced nonlinear optics and low-threshold polariton devices.

title: Writing monolayer oxides with electrons
abstract: Layered metal oxyhalides can be selectively dehalogenated inside a scanning transmission electron microscope, yielding free-standing monolayer oxide sheets and coupling synthesis with atomic-resolution observation.

title: Could your chatbot tip off a scientific rival? It’s possible, researchers say
abstract: AI experts offer tips for keeping sensitive research private

title: Rapid longitudinal flights cause time shifts and Sun compass error
abstract: Many animals use the Sun compass to guide their movement, sometimes over thousands of kilometers. Consistent use of the Sun compass relies on the endogenous clock to track the Sun’s arc, yet animals traveling east-west experience time shifts, potentially causing mismatches between their internal clock and local time. Using GPS, we reveal that Manx shearwaters ( Puffinus puffinus ) experience such shifts during homing flights, generating predictable errors in Sun compass orientation. Use of the Sun compass persists even when shearwaters have access to compass-independent cues during coast following. Our findings provide a new avenue for chronobiology research in the wild, suggesting that rapid longitudinal movements may affect other processes governed by the endogenous clock and that conserved chronobiological mechanisms impose substantial constraints on navigation.

title: Darwin’s atom split
abstract: A whole central nervous system is exposed

title: Giant Magneto-Photoresponse in 2D Room-Temperature Magnetic Semiconductor Heterostructures
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic semiconductor heterostructures serve as an ideal material platform for the exploration of emergent physical phenomena and high-density integrated electronics, owing to the strong magneto-electric-optical coupling at their interfaces. Remarkably, the interfacial engineering also endows the heterosystem with pronounced multifield tunability, facilitating the development of next-generation low-power multifunctional devices. Nevertheless, their practical development remains hindered by low magnetic ordering temperatures and the lack of scalable synthetic methods. Here, we develop a dual precursor-assisted chemical vapor deposition strategy to achieve large-scale synthesis of room-temperature-operable FeSex/WSe2 magnetic semiconductor heterostructures with atomically sharp interfaces. The photoresponse of the as-fabricated heterostructure can be effectively programmed by an external magnetic field, achieving a prominent room-temperature modulation ratio exceeding 50%. Such impressive magneto-photoresponse originates from spin-dependent interfacial charge transfer. Furthermore, the synergistic tunability of photoelectric performance under varying illumination and magnetic fields facilitates the construction of an adaptive enhancement framework for magnetic sensing, which enables optimized low-contrast image recognition and paves the way for advanced in-sensor computing systems. This work not only provides a feasible synthetic route for large-scale preparation of 2D heterostructures, but also sheds new light on the design of multifunctional devices with multifield coupling characteristics.

title: The SDGs need a subjective well-being reality check
abstract: The Sustainable Development Goals aim to improve lives, but it is unclear whether progress on Sustainable Development Goal indicators translates into greater subjective well-being over time. A study of 42 countries found associations in levels, but weak links with year-to-year changes in life evaluations.

title: Phenol-Driven Modulation Enables the Crystallization of Titanium Metal–Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) remain among the most challenging frameworks to synthesize due to the high reactivity of Ti(IV) precursors, particularly when in combination with strongly coordinating phenolate ligands. Phenol is an untapped modulator for MOF synthesis that enabled the formation of a new crystalline Ti-MOF phase, otherwise unattainable through established modulators. We show how transient Ti-phenolate species formed in solution regulate titanium coordination equilibria and demonstrate the broader applicability of phenol modulation for several reported Ti-MOF systems. As a result of phenol modulation, we isolate a previously elusive crystalline titanium ellagate sustainable MOF, TUW-11, composed of monometallic Ti(IV) centers and plant-derived ellagic acid linkers. Three-dimensional electron diffraction, synchrotron X-ray techniques, and scanning transmission electron microscopy reveal a layered microporous framework with 1.1 nm channels. TUW-11 exhibits a narrow band gap, p-type semiconducting behavior, and ligand-centered visible-light photoresponse. These findings demonstrate phenol modulation as a powerful strategy for controlling titanium-phenolate framework formation and expand the synthetic toolbox available for Ti-MOF discovery.

title: Proximity labeling of the Listeria monocytogenes surface reveals pathogen control of a host deubiquitinase
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Listeria monocytogenes navigates a crowded intracellular environment by recruiting host factors to its surface in order to hijack the host actin cytoskeleton for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Although these types of Listeria-host interactions are critical for infection, systematic characterization of this interface has been limited. Here, we implement the biotin ligase split-TurboID to profile host proteins recruited to the surface of L. monocytogenes during intracellular infection. We show that the host deubiquitinase CYLD is enriched at the pathogen surface. While CYLD promotes infection by suppressing innate immunity in macrophages, how L. monocytogenes recruits and appropriates CYLD function in other cell types has remained unclear. We demonstrate that L. monocytogenes uses the secreted effector Internalin C (InlC) to redirect CYLD to M1-linked linear ubiquitin at the bacterial poles. Despite its localization, CYLD does not deubiquitinate bacteria or regulate autophagic clearance in epithelial cells. Instead, CYLD and InlC protect L. monocytogenes from IFN-γ- and RNF213-dependent restriction of cell-to-cell spread. Overall, our work profiling the bacterial surface-host interactome has identified a mechanism by which InlC spatially reprograms CYLD activity to promote cell-to-cell spread in epithelial cells. These findings highlight how L. monocytogenes exploits a host deubiquitinase to perform cell-type-specific functions during infection.

title: Predictive Design Principles for Plasma-Catalysis
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Centralized production of fuels and commodity chemicals emits 1.4–2 Gt CO2 yr–1 and depends on fossil-fuel supply chains that prevent distributed deployment. Nonthermal plasmas offer a path to decentralized, electrified production by generating vibrationally excited molecules, radicals, and ions without bulk heating of gas. Despite this potential, plasma-catalysis remains difficult to design because plasma excitation, surface reaction energetics, and intermediate removal are treated separately, and activity trends do not transfer across chemistries. This perspective develops a quantitative framework connecting nonequilibrium excitation, surface binding energetics, coreactant chemistry, and surface temperature to reaction rates, selectivity, and catalyst stability. Reactions are classified into three kinetic regimes by the balance between intermediate supply and removal rates, each with distinct rate-controlling steps and deactivation modes. Design tools and principles derived from this classification are applied to four example case studies that transfer across chemistries without reparameterization and provide a basis for reactor design at scale.

title: A training-free, domain-extensible LLM-based approach for automated extraction of standardized preparation procedures
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Millions of synthesis procedures have been published, but their meta-analysis, important for identifying successful synthesis patterns, is difficult due to varied reporting structures. Using this information requires converting unstructured text into a precise sequence of actions, which requires understanding domain jargon, a challenge usually addressed by fine-tuning models on labeled data. We present a simple, training-free workflow for laboratory action extraction that works across fields, encoding domain knowledge through explicit action sets and using powerful, readily available Large Language Models, or LLMs. Applied to zeolite synthesis, a widely used class of porous materials, our approach outperforms existing open-source tools and delivers context-aware results with open, locally runnable LLMs. It also matches state-of-the-art, field-specific models in their own domains, highlighting the generalization capabilities of current LLMs. The methodology showcased, along with the open algorithms made available, allow chemists to evaluate action sets, screen LLMs, and digitize laboratory procedures accurately with minimal effort.

title: Translating sulfur flow batteries into deployable systems
abstract: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. Yi-Chun Lu and her team explore how deployment reshapes research priorities and reveals the scientific and engineering bottlenecks that determine technology translation.

title: Tree shrew more closely recapitulates primate spermatogenesis than the mouse in cross-species single-cell transcriptomic analyses
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The rapid evolution of spermatogenesis limits the utility of mouse models for studying human spermatogenesis because some genes are absent or divergent in mice. Primate models face practical and ethical constraints, whereas tree shrews are closely related to primates and suitable for laboratory research. Here we integrate histology and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from human, rhesus macaque, mouse and tree shrew testes to assess the tree shrew as a model of human spermatogenesis. We show that transcriptional landscapes in tree shrew spermatogenic cells, particularly late-stage spermatids, more closely resemble those of primates than mice. Conservation and enrichment analyses identify two core gene modules shared among humans, macaques and tree shrews but distinct in mice. Gene expression trajectories also align between tree shrews and primates, including for genes without murine orthologs. Immunostaining and RNA-FISH support representative expression patterns. These findings define contexts in which tree shrews can complement existing models of human spermatogenesis and male infertility.

title: Angular solar absorption and thermal energy storage seasonally modulate radiative cooling
abstract: Passive daytime radiative cooling materials (RCs) maintain low surface temperatures under sunlight and can reduce building cooling loads and urban overheating. However, RCs with static optical properties overcool in cold seasons, and adaptive RCs proposed to date rely on temperature/humidity to switch their optical/radiative properties. Further, they address either daytime or nighttime response and are subject to ageing and to false switching on mild sunlit winter days. Here, we propose a system to seasonally modulate RCs with angular solar absorption, achieved with L-shaped fins, and with thermal energy storage (TES), implemented with phase change materials (PCMs) and concrete mass. The L-shaped fins have solar-absorptive, equator-facing walls shaded by horizontal eaves, enabling high direct solar absorption only at the low solar elevations of winter, with RC film on all other surfaces. Coupled with TES, the system is an angular-dependent thermal-mass-enhanced radiative cooler (ATMRC). In field campaigns in Western Sydney, the finned RC samples reached winter daytime surface temperatures 6–9 °C above the static RC and up to 11 °C above the unfinned RC + TES, resolving the daytime overcooling that TES alone introduces. The ATMRC with the 8 °C PCM reduced winter dew and frost durations by 56% and 73%, respectively, relative to the static RC. The summer daytime penalty against the static RC was 2 °C. Ray-tracing yields seasonal absorbed fractions of 37% in winter and 21% in summer in Sydney. Effective adaptive RCs therefore require both TES against night overcooling and angular-dependent solar absorption for daytime modulation.

title: Exaiptasia diaphana core microbiome members are lost under climate change conditions despite host thermal tolerance
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. We exposed two lines of the sea anemone, Exaiptasia diaphana, to acute and chronic thermal stress to quantify the impacts on cnidarian physiology and microbiome composition. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs.

title: Deuteration of arenes in D2O exclusively driven by single-atom Pt sites under visible light
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deuterated arenes play crucial roles in medicinal chemistry and materials science (e.g., psychotropic drugs and deuterated OLEDs). However, the desired late-stage deuteration via conventional hydrogen isotope exchange methods always demands expensive isotopic reagents (e.g., D2, C6D6, or C2H5OD), metal complex catalysts, or harsh conditions ( ≥ 120 oC, 20 bar H2). Here, we report a single-atom photocatalytic strategy for efficient deuteration of electron-rich arenes using D2O as the deuterium source. Under visible light irradiation at ambient temperature in an inert atmosphere, a single-atom photocatalyst (Pt1/TiO2) affords high deuterium incorporation across 54 electron-rich arene substrates. The protocol is mild, sustainable, and scalable: gram-scale synthesis of deuterated arenes (11.98 g, 100 mmol) was successfully realized. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catalytically active sites are primarily Pt–O coordinate bonds, whose light-modulated charge distribution facilitates a possible electrophilic platinization pathway for C–H activation before H/D exchange.

title: The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) offer potential advantages for clinical diagnosis over standard large language models (LLMs), yet their utility and safety remain unclear. Here we show, on AIMS-LDR, a long-context diagnostic reasoning benchmark built upon real-world electronic health records, covering six matched model pairs and 12 specialties, that LRMs generate over 34% more false positive diagnoses and show approximately 40% lower reproducibility than their LLM counterparts, while making more accurate primary diagnoses and more clinically relevant differentials. Experiments confirm this trade-off across prompt designs, model hyperparameters, and evaluation paradigms. A structured collaboration model, in which the LRM broadens diagnostic coverage and the clinician verifies reliability, increases diagnostic accuracy by 20% and reduces false positives by 44% in a 15-physician validation study. These results, obtained under controlled retrospective conditions, suggest that pairing LRM reasoning with physician oversight may support safer and more accurate diagnostic decision-making, warranting prospective validation before clinical deployment.

title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells
abstract: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cell.

title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

title: Secondary organic aerosol formation from sequential oxidation of toluene and cresols
source: Earth and environmental sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cresols are important urban emissions that can form multiple oxygen containing condensable vapors when they react with OH radicals in the atmosphere. These molecules contribute to secondary organic aerosols that have strong implications on climate and human health. In this work, we present flow reactor oxidation experiments demonstrating the rapid (sub-second) formation of condensable vapors with up to 10 oxygen atoms from the three cresol isomers (ortho-, para- and meta-cresol) under atmospheric conditions. Our quantum chemical calculations reveal that initial OH additions to the hydroxyl containing carbon atom lead to geminal diol intermediates that are critical to the rapid formation of condensable vapors from cresols and their key oxidation product, 3-methylcatechol. Incorporating these autoxidation mechanisms into model simulations shows that they contribute significantly to secondary organic aerosol composition. These results could explain the strong multi-generational contributions to aerosol from toluene and cresol, enabling a more accurate assessment of their climate and health impacts.

title: Antimicrobial peptides derived from Nemuri induce ribosomal condensation to inhibit translation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antibiotic resistance is a global health threat requiring antimicrobials with alternative modes of action. Growing evidence indicates that bacteria organize key intracellular processes through biomolecular condensates and other forms of spatial organization, yet whether such spatial organization can be exploited as an antimicrobial target remains unclear. Here, we identify intrinsically disordered antimicrobial peptides, generated from the Drosophila sleep-inducing protein Nemuri, that inhibit bacterial growth by targeting ribosomal organization. Mechanistically, these peptides enter bacterial cells without overt membrane disruption and accumulate in ribosome-rich regions, where they bind broadly to RNA and ribosomal surfaces through multivalent interactions. This engagement remodels ribosome-rich regions into condensates with reduced ribosomal mobility, thereby suppressing global protein synthesis and distinguishing these peptides from canonical site-specific ribosome-targeting antibiotics. Furthermore, Nemuri-derived peptides exhibit broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, including activity against drug-resistant pathogens, with low cytotoxicity toward Drosophila and mammalian cells. Together, our findings identify the organization and material dynamics of bacterial ribosomes as a biophysical vulnerability that can be exploited by antimicrobial peptides, revealing how a naturally evolved metazoan host-defense system turns intracellular organization itself into an antibacterial target.

title: CryoET imaging reveals that mitotic spindles are locally organized by microtubule density and Eg5 activity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: When eukaryotic cells divide, a mitotic spindle, composed of microtubule filaments interacting with molecular motors, self-assembles and is responsible for aligning and segregating chromosomes to the opposite daughter cells. Recent structural studies revealed that spindles are composed of short microtubules that do not span the full pole-to-chromosome distance. It remains unclear how these short, disconnected microtubules collectively assemble a bipolar spindle. Using cryo-electron tomography to map microtubule polarity in human spindles, we find that microtubules organize with consistent 8 nm wall-to-wall spacing. Spacing scales inversely with local microtubule density, consistent with organization by density-driven steric interactions, analogous to liquid crystal ordering. We find that the Eg5 motor establishes local antiparallel overlap independently of spindle bipolarity, while a balance of Eg5 and dynein regulates microtubule density to maintain spindle architecture. Together, these findings reveal the mesoscale principles by which cells build complex, self-healing cellular architectures from nanoscale building blocks.

title: Widespread selection of antibiotic resistance within hospital sewers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Environmental microbiomes are sources of diverse antibiotic resistance determinants that can be mobilized and transferred to human pathogens under a selection pressure from antibiotics. Hospital sewers contain more antibiotics than most environments and are thus increasingly recognised as potential arenas for resistance evolution. However, it is unknown if resistance selection occurs there and what the drivers are. Here we show selection of antibiotic-resistant bacteria within Swedish hospital sewers. Evidence include; consistent selection of multiple resistances in Escherichia coli exposed to filtered wastewater from ten hospitals, but not to corresponding municipal wastewaters; in-situ enrichment of resistant over sensitive E. coli from wastewater to sewer biofilms at hospitals, but not at municipal sites; and higher resistance in bacteria collected from hospital sewers than from municipal sites as assessed by culturing and metagenomics. Evidence for drivers includes complete rescue of sensitive E. coli by addition of resistance genes to fluoroquinolones and β-lactams, and cellular effects typical for β-lactams. Measured concentrations by liquid-chromatography-tandem-mass-spectrometry compared to selective thresholds identify ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime as principal selective agents. Antibiotic concentrations and use data allow extrapolation of risks beyond Sweden. Given the absence of detectable selection at municipal sites, mitigations of risks in hospital sewers should be prioritized.

title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
abstract: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.

title: Increasing prevalence and expanding diversity of tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella in China
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The plasmid-mediated tigecycline resistance gene tet(X4) threatens the efficacy of tigecycline. While prevalent in Escherichia coli across diverse ecological niches, its evolutionary trajectory in Salmonella remains underappreciated. Here, we conducted nationwide genomic surveillance of 42403 clinical nontyphoidal Salmonella isolates collected from diarrheal patients in China between 2014 and 2025, of which 102 were tet(X4)-positive. Although the overall prevalence remained low, detection showed a statistically significant upward trend over 2019-2025. Importantly, the newly accrued 2025 data were broadly consistent with short-term forecasts generated by the beta regression model, providing partial support for short-term trend consistency. Genomic analyses showed that tet(X4) remained concentrated in ST34 but was also detected in additional sequence types, including ST469, ST8971, ST11 and one isolate with an unassigned ST, across multiple provinces, indicating broader geographic representation and genetic diversification. Plasmid analyses likewise revealed broader replicon diversity, with the dominant IncHI1A/IncHI1B/IncFIA background accompanied by less frequent IncHI2/IncHI2A, IncI1(Alpha) and IncFIA/IncFIB/IncFIC. Phylogenetic analyses further revealed shared clustering of the dominant plasmid background across host species and bacterial genera, consistent with cross-host and cross-genus circulation.

title: Protease‐Responsive Condensation of Engineered Proteins Drives Tumor‐Targeted T‐Cell Activation
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are fundamental to cell signaling. Extracellular phase separation is emerging as a potent strategy for cell‐specific signaling modulation; however, its application is limited by the lack of control over on‐demand condensate formation. Here, we engineered a masked extracellular phase‐separation platform (Condenstim) enabling tumor microenvironment‐specific condensate formation. To achieve this, we first developed an LLPS‐based system that clusters CD3 and CD28 receptors to assemble synthetic immunological synapses for potent T‐cell activation. By employing a protease‐cleavable linker for site‐specific PEGylation, we sterically shielded the protein building blocks, rendering the platform biologically dormant during systemic circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment, localized proteases cleave the linker, thereby restoring LLPS in situ. This modular design ensures spatially confined and efficient T‐cell activation, leading to robust tumor regression in murine models, both as a monotherapy and in combination with PD‐1 blockade. Our findings establish a generalizable strategy to control extracellular LLPS for both fundamental studies and therapeutic applications.

title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
abstract: ABSTRACT The native chemical ligation (NCL) is a cornerstone of protein synthesis, allowing the assembly of peptide fragments into larger proteins. Ligation auxiliaries extend the scope of NCL beyond cysteine, but fragment ligation at sterically encumbered junctions remained inaccessible. Herein, we introduce a pyridine‐containing ligation auxiliary that allows NCL to proceed at virtually any junction, including reactions at β‐branched amino acids, as well as O ‐glycosylated or O ‐phosphorylated amino acids. Through iteration of the auxiliary scaffold, we revealed a fundamental relationship between the basicity of the pyridine and ligation speed. Surprisingly, the 2‐mercapto‐2‐(4,5‐dimethoxypyridin‐2‐yl)ethyl (MDPE) auxiliary operates over a broad pH range, enabling ligations even in highly acidic conditions. This property was leveraged in the synthesis of dodeca‐phosphorylated peptides from the large RNA polymerase II CTD domain. Additionally, we utilized the MDPE auxiliary for the synthesis of heavily glycosylated segments derived from mucin MUC5AC.

title: Bioinspired Artificial Cilia and Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Biological cilia are prevalent organelles found in a wide range of human organs. Despite their small size, natural cilia feature exquisite and intricate architecture and play an important role in human life. For example, motile cilia in the brain and lung are responsible for fluid propulsion and particle removal. Furthermore, primary cilia in the epidermis and inner ear have sensitive detection capabilities for pressure and sound. Over the last three decades, researchers have created various artificial cilia inspired by the architecture and multifunctional capabilities of natural cilia. Artificial cilia have evolved as a versatile biomimetic platform with promising applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of research advances in artificial cilia. First, the structural and functional features of natural cilia, as well as the key developments in artificial cilia, are outlined. Subsequently, various fabrication strategies, actuation mechanisms, and cutting‐edge applications of artificial cilia are further explored. Finally, the main challenges and future research directions toward realizing artificial ciliary systems that more closely mimic the performance of their natural counterparts are discussed.

title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single‐Atom‐Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite‐free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single‐atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single‐atom‐nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination‐mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non‐equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co‐species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local d ‐band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption‐energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high‐loading Li||LiFePO 4 full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic‐structure regulation in practical LMAs.

title: Scalable and Lithography‐Free Fabrication of High‐Aspect‐Ratio Diamond Nanowires for Photonic and Electrochemical Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT The scalable integration of low‐dimensional diamond nanostructures into advanced technologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by the complexity and high cost of conventional lithography. Here we report a highly scalable, lithography‐free top‐down etching approach to produce densely distributed high‐aspect‐ratio (HAR) diamond nanowires across polycrystalline (PCD), single‐crystal (SCD), and boron‐doped diamond (BDD) substrates, including continuous fabrication on a full 2‐inch wafer. By correlating time‐dependent surface characterizations, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and 3D femtosecond laser tomography, we elucidate an Ag‐initiated, redeposition‐sustained secondary inorganic micromasking process: self‐assembled Ag nanoclusters initiate nanowire formation, while redeposited inorganic residues derived from the carrier wafer and chamber environment sustain anisotropic etching during prolonged reactive ion etching (RIE). The broad versatility of this method is validated through distinct functional demonstrations: PCD nanowires demonstrate a pronounced transition to hydrophobicity; SCD nanowires demonstrate spatial modulation and localized enhancement of ensemble nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) photoluminescence, while finite‐difference time‐domain (FDTD) simulations support nanowire‐assisted optical extraction; BDD nanowires provide an approximately 30‐fold increase in electrochemical double‐layer capacitance (C dl )‐derived accessible electrochemical surface area, achieving a 2.5‐fold enhancement in pollutant‐degradation kinetics with stable electrochemical operation. This study establishes a viable and scalable pathway for integrating diamond nanostructures into advanced sensing, photonics, and electrocatalysis.

title: Modulating Local Electronegativity in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Host–Guest Oxygen Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing high‐performance metal‐free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction remains a major challenge in sustainable energy conversion. Herein, we report a host–guest chemistry strategy based on metal‐free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to significantly enhance the catalytic performance. Unlike conventional COFs that focus primarily on linkage chemistry or heteroatom doping, our approach explicitly leverages molecular‐level design to create tailored binding pockets within the COFs pores, enabling high selectivity and strong interactions with O 2 . A series of fluorene‐based COF hosts with systematically tuned electronegativity are designed and synthesized to strengthen molecular recognition and binding toward oxygen via tailored electronic and structural environments. The optimized material achieves a remarkable half‐wave potential ( E 1/2 , vs. RHE) of 0.78 V, among the highest reported metal‐free COF‐based catalysts. This exceptional performance originates from enhanced host–guest recognition, which effectively facilitates O 2 adsorption while optimizing the stabilization and subsequent dissociation of key reaction intermediates on the active site. Through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, these host–guest interactions promote the optimized adsorption of intermediates and accelerate reaction kinetics. This study provides a new paradigm for the design of high‐efficiency metal‐free electrocatalysts through precise molecular recognition, opening avenues for advanced catalytic systems beyond conventional approaches.
