title: Genomic heterogeneity inflates the performance of variant pathogenicity predictions
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Recent studies have reported unprecedented accuracy predicting pathogenic variants across the genome, including in noncoding regions, using large deep-learning models trained on vast genomic data. To verify and understand the basis of these reports, we systematically evaluated the prediction accuracy of frontier models over single-nucleotide variants, focusing on general models capable of scoring multiple variant types across coding or noncoding regions. Our evaluations reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is severely inflated by mixing variant categories with different baseline prevalences of pathogenic variants. We constructed a benchmark stratified by variant type to identify the best-performing models for each genomic context, determine where reliable predictions remain out of reach, and establish rigorous standards to guide future evaluations.

title: Optimisation of a grid-connected electrolyser: time-ahead dispatch and energy portfolio planning
abstract: This study investigates short-term power dispatch optimisation and long-term energy capacity planning for a grid-connected water electrolysis system (WES). It explicitly accounts for key technical characteristics often overlooked in existing studies, including dynamic specific energy consumption (SEC; incorporating both stacks and balance of plant (BoP)), minimum load, ramping, and usage-based stack degradation. To enable computationally tractable optimisation without sacrificing these key technical aspects that introduce nonlinear dynamics, a two-step approach is adopted. First, nonlinear governing relationships (e.g., between input power and SEC) are derived using a detailed cell-level stack model. Second, these relationships are approximated using piecewise linearisation (PWL) with minimal error. The results show that time-ahead dispatch optimisation significantly reduces total electricity cost relative to constant operation; however, this benefit diminishes at higher required average WES utilisation due to reduced temporal flexibility (i.e., less freedom to shift production), which in turn constrains the effective use of operational flexibility (e.g., ramping). Optimal energy portfolio design is highly sensitive to yearly average WES utilisation and power purchase agreement (PPA) prices. Higher utilisation rates (URs) require increased grid-sourced firming of the power supply, whereas lower utilisation enables greater reliance on variable renewable energy (VRE), albeit with larger contracted capacities, yet remaining economically favourable. Sensitivity analysis further shows that wind PPA plays a dominant role in portfolio design, driven by its higher base cost relative to solar PPA and more consistent generation profile.

title: Minimally invasive topological light manipulation with lensless fiber endomicroscope
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Topological light fields, with their robust properties, offer transformative potential across photonics. However, achieving flexible manipulation and practical deployment of topological light fields in hard-to-reach areas remains challenging. To overcome this limitation, we propose an adaptive topological light endoscopic system (ATLES) and pioneer an integrated transceiver design based on a multi-core fiber, enabling minimally invasive detection with topological light field manipulation. Leveraging the ATLES framework, we reconfigure a 10,000-core fiber into a high-resolution modulator for phase, amplitude, and coherence control. This enables the on-demand creation of both coherent and incoherent topological light fields, tailored in their structures, directly from a bare fiber tip of just 350 μm in diameter. We demonstrate the power of this approach by performing highly precise rotational velocity measurements under endoscopic conditions, achieving a relative error below 0.055%. Our work establishes a versatile platform for the implementation of topological photonics in hard-to-reach areas, thereby paving the way for their application in biomedical imaging and optical computing.

title: Icosahedral-group beam layouts for highly uniform direct-drive laser fusion
abstract: We investigate irradiation uniformity in direct-drive laser fusion using beam layouts generated from the full rotational icosahedral group. By expanding the incident intensity in spherical harmonics, we show the selection rules imposed by exact icosahedral invariance and identify the forbidden multipole degrees. These exclusions are independent of the single-beam profile and therefore remain valid for both delta-function and finite-width beams. Using flat-top and von Mises–Fisher beam profiles, we evaluate the resulting root-mean-square nonuniformity and compare an optimized 60-beam icosahedral layout with the conventional OMEGA 60-beam geometry. For smooth beam profiles, this model predicts substantially lower nonuniformity for the optimized icosahedral layout than for the OMEGA-60 geometry, because exact low-degree cancellation is combined with efficient high-degree attenuation by the beam-profile transfer coefficients. We further examine random beam-weight imbalance and show that optimized high-beam-count icosahedral layouts remain robust over the range studied. These results establish a symmetry-based design principle for low-mode control and improved irradiation uniformity in direct-drive laser implosions.

title: Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
Geopolitical risk and energy poverty in African net energy importers: Localized effects, structural vulnerability, and conditional resilience
Who leads the global gas market? Geopolitics and price transmission between the U.S. and Europe
Circular economy practices and clean energy transition performance: the moderating role of critical mineral circularity and policy stringency among EU energy-intensive firms
Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Translating EU renewable energy community policy under geopolitical constraint: An actor-network analysis of Cyprus
abstract: We use an actor-network concept of translation to examine how EU Renewable Energy Community (REC) policy translates into domestic practice under contested sovereignty, infrastructural isolation, and active geopolitical obstruction. Cyprus is a critical, theory-building case: the EU's last fully isolated grid, occupation of part of its territory by a third state, and Turkish obstruction of both gas exploitation and electricity interconnection make the assumptions embedded in EU policy unusually visible. Drawing on policy documents, twelve interviews and participant observation, we trace how the framework fragments as it moves from supranational design to local implementation. The evidence supports two case-derived hypotheses. The first, presupposition-mismatched translation, holds that compliance fails not for want of will or capacity but because the policy as written presupposes a context that does not exist locally, so translation fragments into competing local interpretations. The second, symmetric foreclosure, holds that where one external mechanism blocks both the domestically prioritised energy-security pathway (gas) and the EU-aligned pathway (interconnected renewable generation), competing local obligatory passage points cancel rather than converge. Their joint product is structural decoupling under material constraint, extending Bromley and Powell's means–ends decoupling to cases where the formal-substantive gap is produced by foreclosure of the prescribed means rather than by organizational choice. The argument is not that RECs cannot exist in Cyprus, but that this decarbonisation initiative receives weak domestic backing for geopolitical rather than technical reasons. We draw implications for green-transition initiatives in other peripheral, geopolitically exposed member states and for differentiated EU implementation guidance.

title: Large language model-guided multi-agent reinforcement learning for low-carbon data center scheduling considering distribution-network constraint
A two-stage real-time equalization control strategy for off-grid multi-electrolyzer systems considering electrolyzer degradation
FASTPolicy: Fairness-aware spatio-temporal adaptive cooperative energy management of the multi-energy microgrid coalition
Household willingness to accept reverse demand response for renewable curtailment mitigation: a choice experiment in South Korea
Integrated energy trading system for three types of coastal-resilient ZEBs with multiple stakeholders of novel flexibility and grid sharing resources
Optimization and assessment of PCM-enhanced energy piles for photovoltaic-assisted geothermal harvesting
Adaptive dynamic planning method for electric vehicle charging stations considering active interaction with EV growth
abstract: Against the backdrop of rapid development in China's electric vehicle (EV) industry, the adequacy of charging infrastructure has emerged as a critical constraint. In this context, the exploration of economical and adaptable charging station (CS) planning methods is paramount. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptive phased planning method for electric vehicle charging stations that considers transformation and expansion, based on system dynamics (SD) theory. The method explicitly accounts for the active interaction between EV ownership and planning results. Firstly, to reflect the interests of CSs, the power grid, and users, the division of phases as well as the transformation and expansion of CSs are incorporated as decision variables in the planning model. Building on this framework, an adaptive dynamic planning method is developed to minimize the combined cost of investment and queuing. Then, a predictive model for EV ownership is formulated based on SD theory to capture the active interaction between EV ownership and planning results. Finally, the immune genetic algorithm is used to solve the above programming model. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively address the challenges arising from the growth in EV ownership and enhance the adaptability and economy of CS planning schemes.

title: Quantum probability-driven decision framework for sustainable electric vehicle charging station placement under cognitive biases
Learning control policies from heterogeneous multi-horizon time series in battery energy management systems
abstract: This paper introduces Representation-to-Decision (R2D), an end-to-end imitation learning framework that maps heterogeneous multi-horizon time-series inputs directly to battery control decisions through modular Temporal Feature Extractors (TFEs) and a shared latent representation, without an explicit load and PV forecasting step. While accurate forecasting improves prediction quality, optimal control performance remains unguaranteed in prediction-then-optimization pipelines; standard Reinforcement Learning (RL) lacks the long-horizon temporal awareness due to short-window observations, even when forecast signals are available as additional inputs. R2D offers a different perspective: rather than forecasting first and deciding second, it learns to decide directly from raw temporal inputs, with control optimality anchored by an aging-aware Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) expert through Behavior Cloning (BC). Benchmarked against six controllers on a high-fidelity electro-thermal battery simulation across five industrial sites, R2D achieves 62--77\% of the global clairvoyant optimum, outperforms the tested Model Predictive Control (MPC) and RL benchmarks, and yields battery degradation nearly identical to its MILP teacher across all five sites. Comprehensive ablation studies over temporal backbone, model size, expert formulation, aging-cost weighting, and horizon configuration confirm that an LSTM encoder with a 15-minute single-step control horizon provides the most robust and deployment-ready configuration, and cross-site and single-factor out-of-distribution tests show that generalization to unseen profiles is profile-dependent, with policies trained on high-activity sites transferring most reliably.

title: Accurate remaining useful life prediction of lithium-ion batteries via capacity curve modeling with attention fusion learning framework
Stochastic flexibility quantification for urban integrated energy systems: Definition, modeling, and computation
Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.

title: Microneedle Patch with Dual Control of Temperature and Drug-Release for Synergistic Chemo-Photothermal Therapy of Melanoma
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Microneedles (MNs) combining chemotherapy and photothermal therapy offer a smart strategy for melanoma treatment but are hindered by the inadequate control of hyperthermia temperature and drug release. In this study, a novel MN patch consisting of a backing layer and porous needle tips was developed. The backing layer is made of the poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-acrylamide) (PNA) hydrogel. The needle tips are made of ethoxylated trimethylolpropane triacrylate, and their pores are loaded with PNA hydrogel containing both chemotherapeutic drug doxorubicin and photothermal agent polydopamine. Leveraging the thermochromic properties of the backing layer, the MN patch can autonomously regulate the temperature of needle tips to lower critical solution temperature of PNA (around 43 °C) upon near-infrared laser irradiation, without the need for external temperature control devices. Combined with the thermosensitive volume change of PNA in needle tips, the MN patch enables on-demand drug release. In vivo anti-melanoma experiments demonstrated a potent tumor-killing efficacy, with a tumor suppression rate of 89.2%. This innovative MN patch integrating temperature self-regulation and on-demand drug release presents a promising alternative for melanoma therapy.

title: Mie Scattering-Enhanced Fluorinated Polyether Ether Ketone Nanofibrous Films for Efficient Radiative Heat Dissipation
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This study develops a high-performance radiative cooling (RC) composite film based on electrospinning fluorinated polyether ether ketone, incorporating titanium dioxide (TiO2) and hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) as functional fillers to achieve exceptional spectral selectivity with a solar reflectance of 96.51% and mid-infrared emissivity of 95.12%. The three-dimensional porous fibrous network endows the film with outstanding RC performance, achieving a maximum sub-ambient temperature reduction of 14.63 °C under direct sunlight and a temperature reduction of 8.66 °C relative to the bare vehicle model in small-scale outdoor vehicle tests, thereby validating the significant cooling advantage of the electrospinning film under real-world service conditions. The synergistic effect of the porous fibrous network and intrinsically low-surface-energy matrix imparts self-cleaning functionality to the film (water contact angle of 151.46° and sliding angle of approximately 5°), while solar reflectance degradation remains below 3% after the aging test, demonstrating long-term outdoor service reliability. EnergyPlus building energy simulations confirmed that the film achieved annual energy savings exceeding 6% in tropical arid cities, with positive net energy savings across the vast majority of global climate regions. This film provides a comprehensive design paradigm for high-performance multifunctional RC materials, with broad application prospects for low-carbon building energy conservation and outdoor thermal management.

title: Band Structure-Engineered Nanopatterned MoS2/Graphene Heterostructures for Low-Noise Broadband Photodetection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Integrating two-dimensional (2D) heterostructures is a promising strategy for high-performance optoelectronics; however, achieving high sensitivity and broadband response while maintaining low-noise operation remains challenging. Here, we report a nanoporous molybdenum disulfide (MoS2)/graphene heterostructure phototransistor fabricated via block copolymer-assisted self-assembly and material-selective etching, which provides a scalable and reproducible approach for large-area fabrication. By employing a precise etching sequence using O2 plasma for graphene and XeF2 gas for MoS2, we successfully realize a periodic nanohole array while preserving interfacial integrity. The resulting nanoporous architecture induces bandgap opening in graphene and introduces a high density of edge states, which enhances trap-assisted photogating in the phototransistor and significantly amplify the photocurrent. As a result, the device exhibits a high photoresponsivity of 24.58 AW–1 and a specific detectivity of 2.33 × 1011 Jones under 405 nm illumination. Notably, the device demonstrates a robust photoresponse in the mid-infrared (MIR) region (≈11 µm), extending beyond the intrinsic bandgap limitation of MoS2 and enabling detection capability spanning from the visible to the MIR regime, compared with previously reported MoS2-based heterostructures operating over narrower spectral ranges. Temperature-dependent measurements confirm that this MIR response originates from genuine optical carrier generation rather than bolometric effects. Furthermore, the nanoporous graphene suppresses excessive dark current via bandgap opening and edge-induced states, enabling improved signal-to-noise characteristics. These results establish nanoporous 2D heterostructures as an effective strategy for ultra-broadband and low-noise photodetection.

title: Axisymmetric perturbations and vertical displacement oscillatory modes driven by fast ions in tokamak plasmas
abstract: Recent progress on the theory and numerical simulations of vertical displacement oscillatory modes (VDOM) in tokamak plasmas is reported. VDOM are driven unstable by energetic particles and can have an impact on plasma disruptions, plasma edge stability and confinement. These modes are a candidate, together with Global Alfvén Eigenmodes (GAE), to explain Alfvén-frequency n = 0 modes driven by fusion alpha particles recently observed on JET (Oliver et al 2026 Phys. Rev. Lett.136 055101). Differences in the physical mechanisms underlying VDOM and GAE are discussed. An analytic dispersion relation that contains both VDOM and ideal-MHD unstable vertical displacements (VDs) is derived. Limits on plasma elongation for stable plasma operation against ideal-MHD VDs are discussed. While VDOM are generally immune against continuum damping, if the wall is brought very close to the plasma boundary and the plasma density remains relatively large up to the last-closed-flux-surface (as in the case of H-mode discharges), the VDOM oscillation frequency may interact with the Alfvén continuum spectrum, giving rise to continuum damping. Specific types of fast ion distribution functions that can provide an instability drive for n = 0 modes are considered. Numerical simulations of n = 0 modes obtained with the NIMROD code are shown, including a preliminary assessment of the fast ion instability drive for these modes.

title: Progress in reactor-core fusion technologies presented at the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference 2025
abstract: This paper provides an overview of the recent progress in reactor-core fusion technologies within the vacuum vessel presented at the 30th International atomic energy agency fusion energy conference held in October 2025 in Chengdu, China, including plasma control, neutronics and nuclear data, tritium technologies, design and development of in-vessel components, related materials and intense neutron sources for material irradiation. Plasma control focusing on achievements for International Thermonuclear Experimental Reactor (ITER) and major fusion research devices are covered and the application of digital twin and Artificial Intelligence are highlighted. Research and Development results from the ITER and current devices to future demonstration fusion power plant reactors are summarized, particularly new findings, data validation, design and analysis tool improvement, properties assessment and technical solutions for critical issues.

title: Summary of the contributions on magnetic fusion experiments (EX) to the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference in Chengdu, People’s Republic of China
abstract: This paper summarizes the contributions presented in the ‘magnetic fusion experiments including validation (EX)’ category at the 30th IAEA fusion energy conference 2025, held in Chengdu, People’s Republic of China, from 13–18 October 2025. Conference materials are available at the FEC 2025 conference website (www.iaea.org/events/fec2025), under the category ‘magnetic fusion experiments including validation (EX)’.

title: Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE) at the 2025 IAEA Fusion Energy Conference
abstract: The paper provides a high-level summary of the contributions given at the 30th International Atomic Energy Agency Fusion Energy Conference (FEC2025) held in Chengdu, China, from the 13th to the18th of October, 2025, under the category ‘Inertial Fusion Energy’.

title: Summary of the theory and modelling contributions at the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference (FEC 2025)
abstract: The contributions in magnetic fusion theory presented at the 30th IAEA Fusion Energy Conference (FEC 2025) are summarized. This summary provides information on novel ideas and briefly reviews the most recent advances along the main avenues of the research, such as plasma integrated modelling, computational physics and application of artificial intelligence, fast ion instabilities, runaway electrons, disruptions, pellets, and some others. Given the current interest in bringing the magnetic fusion to the burning plasma state, the focus of the theory presentations was on burning plasma physics.

title: Scalable Melt-Spun Polyethylene/Boron Nitride Fabric Integrating Radiative and Nonradiative Cooling Effects for Personal Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the escalating global energy crisis and environmental challenges, radiative cooling textiles have emerged as a promising energy-free thermal management solution. However, existing cooling fabrics primarily focus on enhancing optical properties like solar reflectance and infrared emissivity, often neglecting the critical role of nonradiative heat dissipation (conduction and convection) while also facing challenges in scalability, durability, and comfort. To address these limitations, this study presents a scalably manufactured polyethylene/boron nitride (HDPE/BN) composite fabric fabricated via industrial melt spinning and weaving. By uniformly incorporating BN sheets into HDPE fibers, the composite fabric achieves enhanced solar reflectivity (86%) and mid-infrared emissivity (89.3%) due to the high refractive index, efficient Mie scattering, and intrinsic infrared absorption features of BN. More importantly, it exhibits enhanced in-plane thermal conductivity (7.73 ± 0.18 W·m–1·K–1) while maintaining breathability, complementing the nonradiative cooling effects. Experimental results demonstrate that the fabric provides temperature reductions of 3.7 °C (daytime) and 2.7 °C (nighttime) in simulated building cooling tests, and 3.9 °C (daytime) and 1.6 °C (nighttime) in simulated human skin tests. This work highlights the importance of integrating optical and thermal management properties, providing a scalable manufacturing route of high-performance personal cooling textiles for practical applications.

title: Matrix Stiffness Controls Lipid Homeostasis in Human Corneal Endothelial Cells via a Piezo1-PI3K/AKT-mTOR-PPARγ Mechanotransduction Axis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Substrate stiffness is a critical mechanical cue that regulates cellular behaviors, yet its role in governing lipid homeostasis of human corneal endothelial cells (HCECs) remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a polyacrylamide hydrogel platform with tunable stiffnesses (25, 50, and 100 kPa) covering the pathophysiological range of Descemet’s membrane to investigate stiffness-dependent lipid metabolic reprogramming in HCECs. All hydrogels exhibited excellent transparency (>95%) and good biocompatibility. We found that soft substrates (25 kPa) promoted substantial accumulation of neutral lipids and free cholesterol in HCECs. Mechanistically, soft substrates upregulated SREBP1 and its target genes to enhance fatty acid synthesis while suppressing CPT1-mediated fatty acid oxidation, and simultaneously upregulated LDLR and SREBP2 to promote cholesterol uptake and synthesis while downregulating the LXRα-ABCA1/ABCG1 axis to impair cholesterol efflux. Notably, PPARγ emerged as a key regulator of stiffness-dependent lipid homeostasis; its expression was positively correlated with substrate stiffness, and pharmacological activation of PPARγ reversed soft substrate-induced lipid accumulation. Furthermore, the Piezo1-PI3K/AKT-mTOR signaling axis was identified as an upstream mechanotransduction pathway mediating stiffness-regulated PPARγ expression. Analysis of transcriptomic datasets from Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD) patients revealed dysregulation of lipid metabolism genes consistent with our findings. Together, these results demonstrate that substrate stiffness governs HCEC lipid homeostasis through a Piezo1-PI3K/AKT-mTOR-PPARγ mechanotransduction cascade, and that matrix softening promotes abnormal lipid accumulation by reprogramming fatty acid and cholesterol metabolic networks. Our findings establish a mechanistic link between the mechanical microenvironment and lipid metabolism in corneal endothelial cells, providing insights into FECD pathogenesis and a theoretical framework for designing stiffness-tuned biomaterials for corneal endothelial regeneration.

title: Efficient and Stable Red QLEDs via 4-TBP-Doped Hole Transport Layer Engineering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The insufficient charge carrier mobility in the hole transport layer (HTL) and the energy level mismatch with the emissive layer have long been critical factors limiting the electroluminescence performance and carrier balance of quantum dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs). To address this issue, we employed 4-tert-butylpyridine (4-TBP) as a dopant in poly[(9,9-dioctylfluorenyl-2,7-diyl)-co-(4,4′-(N-(4-sec-butylphenyl)diphenylamine))] (TFB) as the HTL. By modulating the highest occupied molecular orbital energy level of TFB and enhancing the hole mobility, 4-TBP doping effectively reduces the hole injection barrier and suppresses interfacial charge accumulation. The optimized TFB:4-TBP HTL significantly improves hole injection efficiency in red QLEDs, leading to a decrease in turn-on voltage from 1.74 V to 1.65 V and an increase in external quantum efficiency (EQE) from 22.21 to 26.47%. Moreover, at an initial luminance of 1000 cd m–2, the QLED with the TFB:4-TBP HTL reaches a T95 operational lifetime of 11,708.67 h, which is 2.4 times longer than that of the undoped one. 1.22- and 1.37-fold improvements in EQEmax are obtained for green and blue QLEDs, respectively. This strategy demonstrates that 4-TBP doping, combined with interface engineering, provides an effective method to achieve efficient and stable hole transport, offering new insights for carrier balance control in solution-processed QLEDs.

title: Application of low-Z materials for enhancing H-mode plasma performance and pulse duration in EAST with full metal wall
abstract: Wall conditioning plays a key role in controlling impurity accumulation and fuel recycling for achieving long pulse, high-performance plasmas in fusion device. In this work, the effects of real-time wall conditioning using low-Z materials—boron (B) and lithium (Li) powders injection—are systematically investigated and compared in the EAST tokamak equipped with a full-metal wall. Continuous boron injection effectively suppresses high-Z impurity accumulation and maintains a low effective charge (Zeff), reducing the core W44+ density peak by up to ∼40%, and enabling reproducible 105 s H-mode discharges. Lithium injection also significantly improves impurity and fuel recycling control, supporting a record-breaking 1066 s H-mode plasma under lithium coating. A rigorous statistical comparison via multivariate linear regression within a shared operational window reveals that real-time lithium conditioning delivers an approximate 26% enhancement in the confinement factor H98 compared to the real-time boron conditioning baseline, while maintaining an equivalent core Zeff. This plasma improvement is accompanied by an order-of-magnitude reduction in lower divertor neutral pressure Plow,div and suppressed edge Dα emissions. Analysis of the plasma profile confirms that real-time Li injection enhances wall pumping to reduce edge density, which steepens the local density gradient within the narrow pedestal region. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of low-Z material-based wall conditioning in improving plasma confinement and extending discharge duration, offering important implications for ITER and future fusion devices.

title: Laser-Fabricated Ordered Tri-Level Hemispherical Microstructures for Flexible Pressure Sensors with Ultrahigh Sensitivity over a Wide Linear Range
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of embodied intelligence and soft robotics demands flexible pressure sensors that simultaneously achieve high sensitivity, a broad linear response range, and excellent long-term stability. However, the inherent compression hardening effect of soft materials imposes a fundamental trade-off between sensitivity and linear range, severely limiting their practical applicability in complex dynamic environments. Inspired by the hierarchical tactile perception mechanism of human skin and guided by Archard’s contact theory, we propose a piezoresistive sensor incorporating an ordered tri-level hemispherical microstructure array. The sensing layer, composed of a graphite powder/multiwalled carbon nanotubes/polydimethylsiloxane (GP/MWCNT/PDMS) conductive composite, is patterned via a rapid, scalable, and mask-free three-dimensional (3D) dynamic focusing laser processing technique. Finite element analysis (FEA) guides the optimization of geometric parameters, confirming that the tri-level configuration exhibits the highest compressibility and the greatest rate of contact area change among single-level, dual-level, and tri-level designs. The sensor operates through a graded deformation mechanism: under low pressure, the smallest hemispheres deform first to rapidly increase contact area, under medium pressure, the intermediate hemispheres engage to sustain sensitivity; under high pressure, the largest hemispheres provide structural support, ensuring continuous contact area expansion over a broad pressure range. Consequently, the sensor achieves an ultrahigh sensitivity of 12.8 kPa–1 over a wide linear range of 0–369 kPa (R2 = 0.998), with fast response/recovery times (20/21 ms) and excellent cycling stability (15,000 cycles). Beyond single-point sensing, we further construct a 4 × 4 sensor array that successfully discriminates spatial pressure distributions, as demonstrated by recognition of “M”-shaped and “U”-shaped loading modules. Practical applications include precise monitoring of finger joint bending angles and real-time plantar pressure distribution during walking and running, and shape-resolved tactile imaging, highlighting its great promise for applications in embodied intelligence, wearable health monitoring, human-machine interaction, and related fields.

title: End-to-End Biomanufacturing of Extracellular Vesicles
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have emerged as next-generation, multispecific, and multifunctional agents across medicine, biotechnology, veterinary science, cosmetics, and nutrition. Their delivery efficiency of therapeutic cargo surpasses that of conventional carriers, and their capacity to simultaneously transport internal cargo and activate multiple recipient cells gives them a therapeutic versatility that no other platform can match. Translating this potential into real-world products depends on integrating process design with product characterization, a link that has not yet been systematically established for EV manufacturing. The functionality of an EV is inseparable from how it is made. EV composition is shaped at every stage of production, from the biology of the producer cell, to upstream microenvironmental stressors, to the operational parameters of downstream isolation and purification. Each of these variables influences the final product quality and functionality, which means that process design is, in effect, product design. While many guidelines, including minimal information for studies of extracellular vesicles (MISEV) and quality by design (QbD), have been reported, they operate at different levels: MISEV ensures the validity of EV characterization, whereas QbD defines how a manufacturer designs, controls, and releases a product. Currently, however, there is no link between them to provide an integrative framework. This manuscript, therefore reviews and proposes a framework for context-of-use–dependent EV biomanufacturing, in which biomanufacturing and bioprocessing parameters are deliberately matched to the intended application. By linking specific process conditions to resultant EV characteristics, and by fine-tuning upstream and downstream operations accordingly, bespoke EVs can be produced for defined therapeutic, diagnostic, or industrial purposes rather than made as a single generic product. Together, this work offers essential guidance for producing EVs at scale and for designing end-to-end bioprocesses that can be tailored to the diverse needs of future EV-based products.

title: An Environmentally Benign and Cost-Effective Modified Graphene Oxide/Sodium Alginate-Based Gel Electrolyte for Practical Quasi-Solid-State Zinc-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Quasi-solid-state zinc-ion batteries (ZIBs) have attracted extensive attention owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and environmental sustainability. Sodium alginate (SA), as a natural polysaccharide, is a promising gel electrolyte matrix for sustainable ZIBs. However, the practical application of SA-based gel electrolytes is limited by insufficient ionic conductivity, unstable electrode/electrolyte interfaces, and uncontrolled Zn deposition. To address these problems, a modified graphene oxide/sodium alginate-based gel electrolyte (TCGSA) was prepared by incorporating TiO2/CaCO3 co-modified graphene oxide (TCGO) and erythritol (ER) into the SA matrix. The synergistic interaction among TCGO, ER, and SA was conducive to the transport of Zn2+ and the homogenization of interfacial ion flux, and the ionic conductivity of TCGSA was 23.8 mS·cm–1. Specifically, the polar TiO2-containing groups in TCGO provided additional Zn2+ interaction sites, while the hydrogen-bonding network formed by ER and SA enhanced the structural stability of the gel electrolyte and inhibited interfacial side reactions. When the TiO2 content in TCGO was 3.3 wt %, the Zn||MnO2 full cell assembled by the TCGSA gel electrolyte delivered a maximum capacity of 483 mAh·g–1 at 0.1 A·g–1 and retained 60.92% of its initial capacity after 1900 cycles at 2 A·g–1. Meanwhile, the Zn||Zn symmetric cell exhibited stable cycling for over 1200 h. The cost of the TCGSA pouch cell was relatively low (only $0.026 mAh–1) according to the estimation of raw material prices, and it was a potential candidate for the large-scale production of low-cost and environmentally friendly quasi-solid-state ZIBs.

title: Sn@C Composite with an Ultra-high Initial Coulombic Efficiency via Interfacial Engineering for Sodium-Ion Battery Anodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tin (Sn)-based anodes are attractive candidates for sodium-ion batteries due to their high theoretical capacity and low operating potential. However, their practical viability is severely constrained by drastic volume changes, unstable solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation, and intrinsically low initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE). Herein, an interfacial regulation strategy to enhance the ICE and cycling stability of Sn-based anodes is proposed. That is, we construct Sn-MOF-derived Sn@C composites with submicron Sn particles uniformly confined in a conductive carbon matrix via hydrothermal synthesis and subsequent pyrolysis. This architecture yields an exceptional ICE of 96.4% (725/752 mA h g–1 at 0.1 A g–1), far surpassing that of commercial Sn powder (77.9%). Mechanistic investigations reveal a reversible stepwise alloying pathway from Sn to Na9Sn4 and subsequently to Na15Sn4, while the carbon matrix promotes a thin, uniform NaF-rich SEI that curbs electrolyte decomposition and Na+ loss. In situ EIS-DRT analysis further corroborates the progressive reduction of interfacial resistances during sodiation–desodiation. As a result, the anode sustains 378 mA h g–1 after 500 cycles at 1 A g–1. A Sn@C-900∥Na3V2(PO4)3 full cell can deliver an energy density of 188 W h kg–1 and retain 107 mA h g–1 over 400 cycles, underscoring the practical feasibility of this high-ICE Sn@C anode.

title: Efficient Hydroxymethanesulfonate Electrosynthesis from CO2 and Sulfite over CuPd1 Single-Atom Alloys
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electrochemical C–S coupling of CO2 and sulfite (SO32–) offers a sustainable alternative for hydroxymethanesulfonate (HMS) synthesis, yet its electrocatalytic selectivity remains far from satisfactory. Here, CuPd1 single-atom alloys (CuPd1-SAA) are developed as a highly efficient catalyst for HMS electrosynthesis, delivering an exceptional Faradaic efficiency of 56.8% and an HMS yield rate of 301.5 mmol h–1 g–1 in an MEA electrolyzer, together with outstanding electrolysis stability for over 200 h of electrolysis. Mechanistic investigations reveal the critical Cu-Pd1 synergy in driving CO2 reduction to *CHOH and C–S coupling of *CHOH with *SO3 for selective HMS generation.

title: Microneedle-Based Oral Mucosal Vaccines: Mechanisms, Challenges, and Emerging Strategies
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Oral mucosal vaccination is a minimally invasive and highly acceptable strategy that can trigger both local and systemic immunity. However, its progress toward clinical use is hindered by salivary washout, the multilayered epithelium, and a tolerance-prone immune environment. Microneedles offer a promising way to overcome these barriers. They deliver antigens beneath the oral surface, place them directly in immune-responsive tissues, and can remain operational in the dynamic, enzyme-rich oral cavity. Recent research shows that microneedles enable precise antigen deposition, stabilize fragile vaccine components, and provide controllable release patterns. Studies using both model antigens and clinically relevant targets suggest that oral microneedle vaccination can induce systemic IgG, mucosal sIgA, and tissue-resident cellular responses. Distal mucosal immune responses have also been observed. These distal responses are consistent with the common mucosal immune system (CMIS), although direct evidence of CMIS-dependent lymphocyte trafficking remains limited. The co-delivery of immunostimulatory materials, adjuvants, or nanoparticle carriers further enhances antigen presentation and helps counteract oral immune tolerance. Despite these advances, several challenges remain. These include clarifying the early immune events in oral tissues, identifying adjuvants suited to the oral environment, and ensuring safety, stability, and user acceptability for clinical translation. Overall, current evidence positions microneedles as a versatile and promising platform for mucosal vaccination. Continued integration of oral immunology with formulation and microneedle design will be essential for moving these systems toward real-world application.

title: Hierarchical Biomimetic Engineering of Transition Metal Dichalcogenide-Based Composites for Electromagnetic Attenuation: Structure-Behavior-Function Relationships and Design Rules
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD)-based composites are increasingly investigated for microwave absorption and electromagnetic interference shielding, yet their attenuation response cannot be explained by composition alone. The spatial arrangement of nanosheets, pores, interfaces, and conductive domains governs wave entry, polarization relaxation, carrier transport, and internal dissipation. Biomimetic materials are nevertheless commonly classified by their resemblance to flowers, nacre, honeycombs, or biological networks, making it difficult to compare structures that perform similar physical roles. Accordingly, a structure-behavior-function (SBF) relationship is used to reassess the field. TMDs are considered adjustable building units whose phase, defects, surface chemistry, and assembly can be tailored while restacking, limited conductivity, and structural instability remain practical constraints. Five recurring strategies are examined: porous architectures that modify wave propagation, heterogeneous interfaces that redistribute charge, oriented channels that direct carrier transport, through-thickness gradients that regulate impedance, and multilevel structures that couple these processes. Reported absorption and shielding results are compared to determine where these structural interpretations are supported and where commonly used descriptors, including filler loading, total porosity, and interface density, remain insufficient. The resulting design rules are function-dependent because high total shielding, strong microwave absorption, and absorption-dominated shielding require different balances among conductivity, polarization, and impedance matching. Quantitative descriptors, multiscale modeling, data-assisted design, reproducible manufacturing, and device-level validation are identified as priorities for moving biomimetic TMD composites beyond morphology-led optimization.

title: Multiamino Polydiacetylene-Mediated Interfacial Engineering of Boron Nitride Nanosheet/Polyimide Composites for Low-Dielectric Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of high-frequency and highly integrated semiconductor devices urgently calls for dielectric materials that combine high thermal conductivity, low dielectric constant, and excellent thermal stability. Herein, multiamino polydiacetylene-functionalized boron nitride nanosheets (BNNS@MAPDA) have been incorporated into a MAPDA-containing polyimide matrix to improve filler–matrix interfacial coupling. The functionalized nanosheets exhibit high aspect ratios, few lattice defects, high yields, and excellent dispersion in the PI-MAPDA matrix. At a filler loading of only 7.5 wt %, the PI‑MAPDA/BNNS@MAPDA‑7.5 composite film achieves an in‑plane thermal conductivity of 1.67 W m–1 K–1, representing a 422% enhancement over pristine PI‑MAPDA. Benefiting from the ultralow polarizability of fluorinated groups and the strengthened interfacial coupling, the nanocomposite simultaneously maintains a low dielectric constant of 2.20 and a low dielectric loss tangent (tanδ) of 0.0066 at 1 MHz, alongside a volume resistivity of 9.7 × 1011 Ω cm. The density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that MAPDA functionalization enhances interfacial affinity and energy transfer, while molecular dynamics (MD) simulations elucidate its influence on thermal conductivity and dielectric properties. The Hashin–Shtrikman (HS) model analysis further confirms the positive role of interface regulation in thermal conductivity enhancement. MAPDA-mediated interphase engineering, through multisite anchoring to BNNS and strong chemical affinity with the PI matrix, provides an effective route to promote interfacial heat transfer while suppressing interfacial polarization at low filler loading. This material provides a promising solution for advanced electronic insulation and packaging applications by successfully addressing the challenge of combining low dielectric constant and high thermal conductivity in microelectronic systems.

title: Dual-Scale Hollow-in-Porous PVDF Composite Films Integrating Broadband Reflectance and Fire Safety for Secure Passive Daytime Radiative Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Passive daytime radiative cooling (PDRC) has emerged as a promising zero-energy thermal management technology for building energy conservation. However, the inherent porosity of polymeric cooling materials renders them highly flammable, which facilitates rapid flame spread and poses severe safety hazards in practical applications. To address these challenges, this study proposes a design strategy of “dual-scale optical and multifunctional chemical integration”, successfully fabricating a dual-scale hollow-in-porous polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) composite film that elegantly integrates broadband reflectance with exceptional fire safety. Specifically, hollow core-shell hybrid fillers (ZIF-8@PA@SiO2) were synthesized by etching ZIF-8 templates with phytic acid (PA), followed by uniform encapsulation within a SiO2 shell. These fillers were subsequently incorporated into a PVDF matrix via a phase-inversion process, yielding a hierarchical dual-scale hollow-in-porous architecture. Benefiting from enhanced Mie scattering induced by this structural design, alongside the synergistic molecular vibrations of polar Si–O–Si and C–F bonds, the resulting film delivers an outstanding solar reflectance of 92.3% and a high infrared emissivity of 94.8%. Under outdoor conditions, the composite achieves a sub-ambient temperature drop of 12.7 °C, while under simulated conditions, it exhibits a temperature reduction of 19 °C relative to the bare substrate. The corresponding cooling powers reach 109.3 and 130.7 W m–2 during the day and night, respectively. Crucially, the incorporation of ZIF-8@PA@SiO2 drastically bolsters the material's flame retardancy. Compared to the pristine substrate, the peak heat release rate (pHRR) and total heat release (THR) are curtailed by 52.8 and 52.4%, respectively. This facile and highly effective fabrication strategy paves the way for the secure and practical architectural deployment of PDRC materials.

title: l -Cysteine-Functionalized MXene Porous Scaffold-Based Phase Change Films for Efficient Thermal Management
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Phase change materials (PCMs) hold great promise for thermal management, yet their low thermal conductivity and liquid leakage severely hinder practical applications. Herein, we designed a high-enthalpy phase change composite film (LMAP) based on l-Cysteine-functionalized MXene (l-MXene) and aramid nanofibers (ANFs). l-cysteine was bonded to MXene via covalent and coordination bonds, and further crosslinked with ANF through hydrogen bonds to form layered aerogel films with a porous scaffold structure, which was subsequently impregnated with polyethylene glycol (PEG). The unique porous layered architecture of LMAP-20 achieved a PEG loading of 86.71%, a phase-change enthalpy of 169.33 J/g, and a tensile strength of 17.26 MPa for favorable energy storage performance. Moreover, l-MXene nanosheets endowed LMAP-50 with a high thermal conductivity of 1.58 W/(m·K), which enabled outstanding thermal management and reduced the operating temperature of the LED chip by 21.4 °C. These results suggest that the l-MXene/ANF porous scaffold holds great potential for fabricating phase change composites with high thermal conductivity and suppressed leakage, which could be applied for efficient thermal management in advanced electronic devices.

title: A Pyrrole–Pyridine-Embedded Buckybowl: Synthesis and Application for Rapid Sulfur Mustard Imaging
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Buckybowls, also known as π-bowls, have attracted growing research interest due to their unique curved π-surfaces and associated properties. However, the development of this field faces challenges, primarily the need for reliable synthetic strategies and more demonstrated practical applications. In this work, we have synthesized a pyrrole/pyridine-embedded buckybowl, triazahomosumanene (TAHS), through a “twisted precursor → notched shallow bowl → deep bowl” strategy for the progressive accumulation of high strain energy. TAHS exhibits highly acid-sensitive photophysical properties: substoichiometric protonation induces dramatic fluorescence changes, including a large bathochromic shift (Δλmax = 110 nm) and significant emission enhancement, features not observed for conventional pyridine-based polycyclic aromatics. Further investigations identified TAHS as a fluorescent probe for sulfur mustard with a fast response (5 s), high sensitivity (LOD < 100 nM), and high stability, capable of imaging in both live cells and mice. This work establishes a paradigm for the molecular design and functional application of curved aromatic systems.

title: Ironing out oxygen instability
abstract: Oxygen redox in layered-oxide cathodes could facilitate the development of high-energy sodium-ion batteries, but poor reversibility has limited its practical application. Now, an iron-mediated redox strategy offers a pathway to substantially improving oxygen-redox reversibility.

title: Tuning Superconductivity and Topological Bands in Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–C Medium-Entropy Carbides by Valence Electron Concentration
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The search for unconventional superconductors is a hot topic in materials science and condensed matter physics, yet remains challenging. Here we report a series of medium-entropy carbides (MECs) within the Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–C system with finely tuned valence electron concentration (VEC). Through VEC engineering, the type-II Dirac points are deliberately shifted from approximately 0.19 eV below the Fermi level in the base composition Ta0.25Nb0.25Hf0.25Zr0.25C to within 6.7–59.1 meV of the Fermi level in the optimal composition Ta0.1875Nb0.1875Hf0.3125Zr0.3125C. All five compositions form single-phase rock-salt structures and exhibit type-II bulk superconductivity with TcMid ranging from 2.2 to 4.9 K. Among these, the equimolar Ta0.25Nb0.25Hf0.25Zr0.25C composition exhibits the highest Tc of 4.9 K, with μ0Hc2GL = 1.16 T, μ0Hc1(0) = 65.9 Oe, and ΔC/γTc = 1.16, alongside excellent stability in acidic/alkaline environments and under pressures up to 52 GPa. Our findings establish VEC engineering as a potentially transferable strategy for bridging topological band physics with superconductivity in medium/high-entropy ceramics, positioning this MEC family as a candidate platform for investigating topological superconductivity in disordered systems.

title: Hyperlocal sensing and inverse modeling reveal community impacts of urban air pollutant emissions
abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA—an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure—our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ∼33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (∼10 monitors; ∼1 site per square kilometer, compared with 6.7 sites per square kilometer in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.

title: Engineering bacterial morphology through MreB remodeling enhances one-carbon metabolism for sustainable bioproduction
abstract:
The actin-like cytoskeletal protein MreB controls bacterial cell morphology, yet whether engineered modulation of MreB-associated architecture can improve microbial metabolism remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a chemical-genetic platform in
                    Escherichia coli
                    combining an engineered MreB variant (A53R) that remodels cellular morphology with A22-mediated perturbation of MreB dynamics. MreB(A53R) reshaped cell morphology and engaged an RpoE-Cra-GadE regulatory network associated with cellular adaptation, which remodeled electron transport, redirected carbon flux toward NADPH-generating pathways, and reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS). Consequently, engineered strains exhibited enhanced formaldehyde tolerance and efficient assimilation of methanol and other C1 substrates. Acute A22 treatment recapitulated the morphological alteration but failed to induce metabolic rewiring, revealing a two-stage adaptive response involving immediate physical adaptation associated with cell envelope reinforcement and long-term transcription-dependent metabolic adaptation to persistent morphological remodeling. The analogous V45R mutation in the native methylotroph
                    Bacillus methanolicus
                    partially recapitulated the improved C1 utilization phenotype, supporting the transferability of MreB-based morphological engineering. Collectively, these findings establish MreB-mediated morphological engineering as a strategy to couple cellular architecture with central carbon and redox metabolism and provide a framework for engineering robust microbial chassis for C1 bioconversion.

title: Near‐Infrared Imaging of H 2 O 2 in Plants With Nanosensors Under Environmentally Changing Conditions
abstract: ABSTRACT Optical sensors are powerful tools to monitor biological systems. However, their practical deployment is often limited by environmental interferences such as autofluorescence, mechanical motion, and fluctuating illumination. These challenges are particularly pronounced in plants because they require and use light, which has impaired the use of (fluorescent) sensors for plant stress signals such as H 2 O 2 . Here, we present a ratiometric sensing platform that overcomes these limitations by integrating three spectrally distinct components: 1) an H 2 O 2 sensor based on aptamer modified near infrared (NIR) fluorescent single walled carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs, ∼1000 nm), 2) a stable NIR reference based on polyethyleneglycol modified Egyptian Blue nanosheets (EB–NS, 900–955 nm) and 3) a visible (VIS) signal (∼641 nm) to correct for the NIR autofluorescence tail of plants (>835 nm). This ratiometric approach enables robust signal correction under relevant perturbations, including leaf rotation and wind‐induced motion. Furthermore, it allows continuous H 2 O 2 monitoring under dynamically varying illumination conditions (>300%), resulting in a 75% enhancement in signal contrast compared to single‐channel detection. By spectrally resolving nanosensor signals and endogenous plant autofluorescence, this strategy enables in vivo monitoring of stress‐induced H 2 O 2 under realistic environmental conditions. It establishes interference‐resistant optical sensing and advances field‐deployable nanosensor technologies for precision agriculture.

title: Maleimide‐Functionalized Conjugated Polymers Enable Covalent Biotic–Abiotic Integration to Boost Microbial Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Integrating advanced conductive materials into microbial electrosynthesis systems is a powerful paradigm for merging abiotic performance with biotic specificity, facilitating sustainable transformation of organic waste and carbon dioxide into value‐added chemicals. The regulation of biotic‐abiotic hybrid interfaces in biohybrids is crucial for improving surface microbial abundance, enhancing electron injection, and increasing electrosynthesis production. Herein, maleimide‐functionalized conjugated polymers (p(mNDI‐gT2)) were employed to construct robust, covalent bio‐interfaces via in situ click reactions with cytochrome thiol groups of Shewanella oneidensis , resulting in a doubling of bacterial adhesion. Moreover, intimate contact and binding interactions drastically reduce interfacial resistance and boost electron injection. As a direct consequence of this optimized architecture, the system achieved a 23‐fold increase in electron transfer and a 6‐fold improvement in electrochemical reduction relative to bare S. oneidensis . Furthermore, it obviously outperformed the non‐covalent group, yielding a 2‐fold enhancement in total charge output and a 2‐fold increase in succinate yield. Molecular docking simulations and proteomic analysis collectively reveal that p(mNDI‐gT2) not only facilitates efficient charge transfer but also predominantly upregulates the expression of key respiratory and bio‐interface protein complexes. Fundamentally, this covalent biotic–abiotic interface transcends traditional bulk‐adsorption methods, shifting the paradigm from simple microbial coating to molecular‐level interface engineering.

title: Engineering Li + Transport in Ni‐Rich Layered Cathodes Toward Homogenization
abstract: ABSTRACT Nickel‐rich layered oxide (NRLO) cathodes (Ni≥80%) are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries with energy densities exceeding 300 Wh kg −1 , but suffer from rapid degradation under deep delithiation, including phase transitions, microcracking, and surface reconstruction. These failure modes are increasingly recognized to be coupled through heterogeneous Li + transport across multiple length scales. Here we show that spatial variations in Li + transport originate from atomic, structural, and interfacial factors and ultimately evolve into macroscopic chemo‐mechanical degradation. On this basis, we introduce transport homogenization as a unifying design principle for regulating Li + transport in NRLO cathodes. Within this framework, diverse material engineering strategies, including bulk structural design, interfacial transport engineering, and dynamic transport regulation, are interpreted from a common transport‐centered perspective. We further summarize emerging characterization approaches for quantifying transport heterogeneity and discuss future opportunities for establishing predictive cross‐scale design principles. Overall, this review establishes a transport‐centered framework that unifies degradation in NRLO cathodes and provides a mechanistic basis for rational design of next‐generation high‐energy‐density cathode materials.

title: Coupled carbonate-shale thallium isotopes reveal the evolution of deep-marine anoxia during the end-Permian mass extinction
abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth’s history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

title: The nonsense-mediated decay RNA-surveillance pathway facilitates the hypoxia response by C. elegans
abstract:
Hypoxia (decreased O
                    2
                    ) induces physiological, metabolic, and behavioral changes. The major hypoxia response pathway is conserved from nematodes to mammals and is driven by activation of the HIF (hypoxia inducible factor) family of transcription factors. Despite a fundamental role of the HIF pathway in regulating cellular homeostasis in response to hypoxic stress, interactions between the HIF pathway and cellular quality control pathways are largely unknown. Using an unbiased genetic screen, we found that in
                    C. elegans
                    nonsense-mediated decay (NMD), an evolutionarily conserved mechanism of RNA surveillance, acts in parallel to HIF-1 to selectively enhance specific aspects of the response to HIF-1 activation, possibly through coregulation of a distinct subset of HIF-1–up-regulated genes. Our findings reveal a functional integration between oxygen sensing and RNA surveillance and establish NMD as a key regulator of specific aspects of the HIF-1–driven transcriptional program and physiological response.

title: Atomic-scale facet-defect coupling enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn 2 S 4 for reductive photocatalysis
abstract:
Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we report a facet-defect coupling strategy that enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn
                    2
                    S
                    4
                    through preferential exposure of high-index {102} facets. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the {102} facets simultaneously have a more negative conduction band minimum and intrinsically lower sulfur vacancy formation energy than conventional {110} facets, thereby coupling enhanced reduction thermodynamics with spontaneous defect generation. Guided by these predictions, an ethanol-glycerol–mediated solvothermal strategy was developed to stabilize the high-energy {102} facets via surface-energy regulation. Combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and ultrafast transient absorption analyses demonstrate that the facet-induced sulfur vacancies act as long-lived electron-trapping centers, promoting electron localization, suppressing charge recombination, and prolonging carrier lifetime. As a result, the engineered ZnIn
                    2
                    S
                    4
                    exhibits substantially enhanced catalytic activity across representative multielectron transformations, including H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    photosynthesis, H
                    2
                    evolution, Cr(VI)/U(VI) reduction, and perfluoroalkyl substance defluorination. This work establishes facet-defect coupling as a general strategy for regulating electron accumulation and carrier behavior to advance reductive photocatalysis at the atomic scale.

title: Reorienting hydrolysis reaction toughens interface for 27.2% durable perovskite photovoltaics

title: Harmonic brightness oscillations point to magnetar giant flares in rare short gamma-ray bursts
abstract: Kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) have been observed in a few rare gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), but their physical origin remains uncertain. We reanalyze the two short GRBs with reported kilohertz QPOs, GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A, and find evidence for possible harmonic-like organization around a characteristic frequency scale near 360 hertz. The similar harmonic-like pattern in GRB 910711 and in the confirmed magnetar giant flare (MGF) event GRB 200415A, including features extending above 4 kilohertz, points to timing phenomenology on frequency scales relevant to magnetar oscillation modes. The temporal and spectral similarities between the two events and the difficulty of explaining these features in merger-driven scenarios favor an MGF-like interpretation of GRB 910711. This timing phenomenology may therefore provide an additional observational handle, complementary to spectral, temporal, and localization information, for distinguishing rare MGF-like transients from merger-driven GRBs.

title: A unified lattice–surface engineering strategy stabilizing oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes for all-solid-state batteries
abstract:

Here we report a “coat–sinter–wash” synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a “chemical rivet” and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g

title: Ultrafast singlet–triplet intersystem crossing gated by nonrelativistic nuclear dynamics
abstract: Transitions between electronic states of different spin multiplicities, known as intersystem crossing (ISC), are of fundamental importance in optoelectronics and materials chemistry. ISC has traditionally been viewed as directly driven by spin–orbit coupling (SOC), a relativistic interaction that enables spin-forbidden transitions. Recent studies suggest that vibronic interactions can modulate spin-orbit coupling and induce enhanced mixing between electronic spin states, enabling efficient ISC at specific nuclear configurations. Despite the recognized importance of vibration–spin-orbit coupling, direct manipulation of ISC dynamics through controlled nuclear motions remains challenging. Here, using ultrafast pulse-sequence spectroscopy, we accelerate ISC by nearly three orders of magnitude, reducing its timescale from 1.3 ns to 1.4 ± 0.2 ps. This dramatic enhancement is achieved by selectively tuning vibrational motions in the singlet excited state of the chalcone (E)-3-(4-(dimethylamino)phenyl)-1-(2-methoxyphenyl)prop-2-en-1-one (E-DMPO). Photoexcitation activates benzene-skeleton vibrations that drive the singlet excited state toward geometries near the singlet–triplet crossing region, resulting in rapid and efficient singlet-to-triplet population funneling. These results demonstrate that SOC, although an essential prerequisite for ISC, is not the sole determinant of ISC rates. Instead, nuclear dynamics—an intrinsic nonrelativistic factor—can critically regulate the accessibility of singlet–triplet crossing regions and thereby dominate the ISC kinetics. In other words, nuclear motion can effectively gate ISC. This insight suggests promising molecular- and vibrational-design strategies, beyond the conventional approach of enhancing SOC through heavy-atom incorporation.

Hydroaminomethylation offers a one-pot alternative, but heterogeneous catalysts have long struggled to combine high linear regioselectivity with chemoselectivity due to mismatched kinetics and unselective hydrogenation. title: Temperature-gated active salt secretion enables stable photothermal evaporation
abstract: Photothermal evaporation offers a sustainable solution for brine and seawater desalination, yet its long-term operation is fundamentally limited by salt accumulation arising from diffusion-limited ion transport, especially under high evaporative flux. Here, inspired by the active salt secretion of the mangrove, we develop a temperature-responsive evaporator that actively regulates ion transport through temperature-gated channel dynamics for stable high-flux evaporation. By integrating thermoresponsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) within an ordered reduced graphene oxide-carbon nanotube architecture, the system achieves reversible contraction and swelling with a ratio of 87%, enabling continuous water replenishment during heating and efficient expulsion of concentrated brine upon cooling. This salt secretion process accelerates salt backflow by over 2 orders of magnitude compared with conventional diffusion-driven transport, effectively renewing the evaporation surface and sustaining stable high-flux water collection (∼3.40 kg m−2 h−1) under diverse saline conditions and solar intensities. By replacing passive structural optimization with active transport regulation, this work establishes a new strategy for salt management in photothermal desalination and adaptive interfacial transport systems.

title: High-order nanofluidic spiking encoding
abstract: High-order memristor is needed in neuromorphic engineering for sophisticated neural encoding. Progress has been made in solid-state memristor with electronic dynamics, which, however, presents a significant disparity with the ionic-chemical signaling in the human brain. Herein, we realize high-order nanofluidic spiking encoding based on synergizing the high porosity for non-linear ion transport, light responsibility for optical sensing, and catalytic chemistry for biological perception of a multifunctional covalent organic framework under nanoconfinement. The unique multimodal responses make possible the co-encoded spiking by electricity, light and real neurotransmitter glutamate in the physiological media, leading to the significantly enriched synaptic plasticity towards high-order spiking encoding behaviors, i.e. the rate encoding, time-to-first-spike encoding, rate and temporal fusion encoding, and history-dependent spiking encoding. It is expected to be a starting point for high-order nanofluidic spiking encoding.

Multi‐Hydrogen Adsorption as a Dynamic Electronic Gate for Ultrafast Interfacial Charge Transfer
abstract: ABSTRACT Reactive materials operate under dynamically evolving adsorption environments, yet how cooperative adsorbates reshape interfacial electronic structure and charge‐transfer kinetics remains poorly understood. Here we show that multi‐hydrogen adsorption can function as a dynamic electronic gate that reprograms interfacial charge‐transfer energetics. Using a sulfur‐rich amorphous CoReS 2+x cocatalyst as a model system, we demonstrate that abundant unsaturated sulfur sites enable cooperative multi‐hydrogen adsorption, which induces spontaneous electron delocalization and generates an electron‐deficient interfacial state. This adsorption‐driven electronic redistribution reverses the thermodynamic directionality of electron injection from CdZnS, converting an originally endothermic process into a spontaneous one. Femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy further reveals that the gated interface accelerates interfacial electron transfer to the ultrafast regime, in agreement with first‐principles calculations. The resulting a‐CoReS 2+x /CdZnS system achieves highly efficient photocatalytic hydrogen evolution from biomass‐derived formic acid with an apparent quantum efficiency of 67.8%. More broadly, these findings establish multi‐adsorbate‐induced electronic gating as a general mechanism for dynamically programming interfacial charge transfer in catalytic and energy‐conversion materials operating under realistic reactive environments.

title: Double-layer liquid-surface printing of soft films for flexible electronics
abstract: Soft thin films are essential platforms for developing flexible electronics. However, producing thin films with uniform thickness, free residual stress while often followed by a subsequent defect-free transfer at high yield remains a significant fabrication challenge. Here, we present a liquid-surface printing technique that enables the fabrication of highly uniform, soft, thin films by leveraging controlled spreading of 3D-printed polymeric ink droplets on a double-layer immiscible liquid substrate. The inherent smoothness of the liquid surface together with the self-leveling-driven uniformity of the immiscible liquid layer yields precise control over ink droplet spreading and produces highly uniform soft films free of structural defects or surface irregularities. These films can be programmably transferred onto curvilinear substrates because of the fluidic nature of the underlying liquid substrate and its weak van der Waals interactions with the films while maintaining conformal contact. We demonstrate the versatility of this printing approach by fabricating a broad variety of geometric patterns and local features and also validate its robustness by their extensive mechanical and electrical performance measurement. We further fabricate flexible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags and conformally deploy them to the “skin” of food or food packaging with diverse curvatures for real-time spoilage monitoring, showcasing this technological capability and potential for fabricating flexible and conformable electronics.

title: Structure of vesicular stomatitis virus L-P-N 0 complex by cyro-electron microscopy
abstract:
The large protein (L) of nonsegmented, negative-strand RNA viruses, a viral order that includes rabies, Ebola, Nipah, and respiratory syncytial viruses, catalyze RNA-dependent RNA polymerization on nucleocapsid-sheathed RNA templates. L coordinates two distinct processes: messenger RNA (mRNA) transcription and genome replication. During transcription, L catalyzes cotranscriptional mRNA capping, methylation, and polyadenylation. The additional activities are not required during genome replication; instead, RNA synthesis is coupled to encapsidation by soluble nucleoprotein (N
                    0

                    CTD
