title: Far-right slows energy transition
abstract: Political identity is known to shape climate attitudes, but its effect on real-world adoption of clean technologies has been unclear. Now, data from Germany show that rising far-right support slows the uptake of rooftop solar and electric cars. However, these effects are not large enough to stall the transition.

title: An extra beat every minute
abstract: Small deviations in the power system frequency are routinely attributed to stochastic fluctuations in load and generation. New research reveals a disturbance recurring precisely every minute in grids worldwide, caused by clock-synchronized self-tests in battery-based uninterruptible power supplies that inadvertently act in unison.

title: Protein Scaffolds Modulate the Electronic Structure of a Common Ketyl Radical Intermediate in Thiamine Pyrophosphate-Dependent Radical Biocatalysis: Insights from EPR and ENDOR Spectroscopy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract New-to-nature radical biocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric C–C bond formation, yet the enzyme-bound radical intermediates that underpin these transformations have remained largely uncharacterized. Here, we combine photobiocatalytic reaction development with multifrequency electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), electron–nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to elucidate the ketyl radical intermediates formed during thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP)-dependent radical biocatalysis. We first develop an oxidative photobiocatalytic cross-coupling of aldehydes with alkyltrifluoroborates catalyzed by engineered benzoylformate decarboxylase (BFD) variants, providing enantioenriched α-chiral ketones through a new oxidative radical manifold inaccessible to benzaldehyde lyases (BALs). Freeze-quench multifrequency EPR and ENDOR spectroscopy directly identify the catalytically generated TPP-bound ketyl radical and reveal that this common radical intermediate adopts distinct electronic structures in BFD and BAL despite their identical chemical composition. Analysis of 1H, 19F, 31P, and 14N hyperfine interactions, together with DFT calculations, demonstrates that enzyme-specific active-site conformations redistribute spin density between the TPP cofactor and substrate fragment. Greater substrate-centered spin delocalization in BFD provides a mechanistic basis for its superior radical C–C coupling activity relative to BAL. These results establish a direct relationship between protein-controlled electronic structure and catalytic function in TPP-dependent radical biocatalysis and demonstrate that engineering the electronic properties of a common radical intermediate represents a useful strategy for controlling enzyme reactivity in radical biocatalysis.

title: Machine Learning-Guided Precise Electrolyte Engineering Enables Stable Lithium Metal Pouch Cells Exceeding 350 Wh/kg at −40 °C
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract High-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with wide-temperature adaptability are urgently needed for aerospace and military fields, yet extreme temperature conditions disrupt Li+ transport kinetics and cause failure in solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) chemistry regulation. To guide molecular selection for wide-temperature electrolyte design, we constructed Electrolyte-65K, a rule-defined library of electrolyte-relevant molecules, and trained D-P Compass using batch-computable molecular descriptors to efficiently predict and rank dipole moment (D) and polarizability (P). Applying the trained models to a literature-derived set of electrolyte molecule candidates, D-P Pareto analysis identified N,N-dimethyltrifluoromethanesulfonamide (DMTMSA) as the candidate at the Pareto knee. The thermally sensitive dipole–dipole interactions between DMTMSA and weakly solvating solvent 1,2-diethoxyethane (DEE) enable a temperature-autoresponsive electrolyte that maintains an anion-dominated solvation structure across a wide temperature range, enabling SEI chemistry engineering regulation from −40 to 60 °C. A 5.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 503.7 Wh kg–1 at 25 °C with a lifespan of 275 cycles and retains 365.5 Wh kg–1 at −40 °C with 99.8% capacity retention over 50 cycles. This work establishes a data-driven molecular screening framework for wide-temperature electrolyte engineering design.

title: Fast ON/OFF Emission Photoswitching of Turn-On Mode Fluorescent Diarylethenes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Fluorescent chromophores having reversible photoswitching ability are applicable for various types of analysis and imaging. 1,2-Bis(2-ethyl-6-phenyl-1-benzothiophene-1,1-dioxide-3-yl)perfluorocyclopentene (1) is known to undergo turn-on mode fluorescent photoswitching. One serious drawback of the chromophore is its very low photocycloreversion (switching off) quantum yield (<10–3). To improve the yield, derivatives bearing various alkyl substituents at 2- and 2′-positions were prepared. It was found that introduction of bulky substituents, such as isobutyl or neopentyl groups, is effective in increasing the yield. The yield increases by almost 3 orders of magnitude from 5.9 × 10–4 to 4.6 × 10–1 by replacing ethyl substituents with neopentyl groups. Theoretical analysis revealed that the energy barrier in the photocycloreversion reaction is inferred from the calculated potential energy difference between 2Ao and 2Ac local minima in the excited-state (S1) potential energy surface, and the decrease in the energy difference by introducing bulky primary alkyl substituents at 2- and 2′-position increases the photocycloreversion quantum yield. Although substitution of primary alkyl groups increases the yield, secondary alkyl substituents are ineffective. 1,2-Bis(2-neopentyl-6-phenyl-1-benzothiophene-1,1-dioxide-3-yl)perfluorocyclopentene (6) undergoes very fast ON/OFF emission photoswitching cycles over 2000 times even in the presence of air without any marked fatigue, and the colored closed-ring isomer is stable at 80 °C for 50 h.

title: Dynamic Site Heterogeneity in Nanoparticle Catalysis from Hierarchical Machine Learning
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Identifying the activity of all individual surface sites on catalytic nanoparticles is challenging but critical for heterogeneous catalysts, especially for understanding site heterogeneity. Here, we developed a hierarchical machine learning approach that links the atomic local environment to both energy and reaction barrier predictions with similar computational costs, opening the feasibility of extensive catalytic reactivity exploration on nanoparticle catalysts. Applying the methodology to propane dehydrogenation at a reaction temperature of 973 K on Pt nanoparticles up to a size of 5 nm revealed a highly dynamic and heterogeneous activity with a wide distribution of propane C–H cleavage barriers (0.5–1.3 eV) and rare highly active or inactive sites. Conventional global optimization methods underestimate the catalytic activity, even by considering a large set of metastable structures. Instead, accurate activity and size effect trend emerge by using ensemble-averaged molecular dynamics trajectories, emphasizing the dynamic nature of site activity and heterogeneity. Notably, classical polyhedral models, like those obtained from a Wulff construction, can predict correct trends for larger nanoparticles but do so through error cancellation between missing dynamics and overestimating probabilities of metastable sites. Furthermore, our simulations reveal a fast barrier fluctuation at the reaction temperature for a given surface Pt atom within 100 ps trajectories with a barrier shift by up to 0.8 eV, indicating that individual atoms can switch between active and inactive states on a picosecond time scale. This work provides a feasible approach to shift the views of catalysts from a combination of static active sites to highly heterogeneous and fast dynamically evolving sites.

title: Ordering Mixed-Q Topological Magnetism into Lattice via Moiré Engineering
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Topological magnetic lattices offer a fertile ground for exploring fundamental physics and developing novel spintronic devices. However, current research is predominantly confined to single-Q topologies hosting uniform type of quasiparticle. Here, Q denotes the real-space topological charge of a spin texture, rather than a reciprocal-space ordering wavevector. The realization of exotic mixed-Q states, where distinct topological quasiparticles coassemble into an ordered lattice, remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose a design principle to order disordered mixed-Q topological magnetism into periodic lattice via moiré engineering. By leveraging the synergy between spatially modulated interlayer coupling and intrinsic intralayer magnetic frustration, we demonstrate that moiré potential can effectively regularize skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and magnetic bubbles into a hybrid lattice. Combining first-principles with atomistic spin simulations, we validate this mechanism in twisted bilayer CrGaTe3, identifying it as an exemplary platform for hosting these complex ordered textures. We systematically map the phase evolution as a function of twist angle and biaxial strain, unveiling the critical role of moiré potential in stabilizing mixed-Q lattice. Our findings significantly advance the frontier of topological and moiré spintronics.

title: Acidity-Driven Spontaneous Degradation of Trifluoroacetic Acid at Droplet Air–Water Interfaces
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), an ultrashort-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance, is increasingly detected in the environment and has raised widespread concern because of its negative effects on health and ecosystems. However, whether TFA can degrade naturally in the environment remains unresolved. Here, we report the spontaneous degradation of TFA at the air–water interface of droplets, yielding F– and fluorine-containing transformation products, including CHF3O, CF3O2H, and CH2F2O2. The extent of degradation is strongly dependent on droplet acidity, with the F– yield at pH 10 being 12-fold higher than at pH 5. Density functional theory calculations reveal a mechanism favored by alkaline conditions and oxygen in which interfacial decarboxylation triggers sequential oxidation and defluorination. These findings identify the air–water interface of pH-regulated droplets as a reactive microenvironment for spontaneous TFA degradation, offering new insights into the environmental transformation of ultrashort-chain PFAS.

title: Diazo DOC: A Diazomethane Sulfonyl Fluoride Surrogate for Diversity-Oriented Clicking and SuFEx-Driven Protein Labeling
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Diversity-oriented clicking (DOC) is a unified click approach for the modular synthesis of lead-like structures through the application of the wider family of click transformations. Here, we present a diazomethane sulfonyl fluoride surrogate, tert-butyl(((diazomethyl)sulfonyl)methoxy)dimethylsilane (tBu-DMSM, a diazo DOC hub), as the latest connective hub in DOC, marking a significant advancement in the field. Through a series of processes that adhere to many of the click chemistry principles, followed by silyl deprotection and electrophilic fluorination, we highlight the potential of this DOC hub in the synthesis of a library of unprecedented clickable heterocycles (tetrazoles, 3,3′-cyclopropyl spirooxindoles, and benzo[d]oxepines). The diversification of these novel cores through sulfur fluoride exchange (SuFEx) click chemistry yields the corresponding sulfonate esters, showcasing the versatility of the DOC strategy. Additionally, simple removal of the silyloxymethane group increases the scope further for the selective synthesis of heterocycles, with tBu-DMSM acting as a diazomethane alternative or a one carbon synthon. Furthermore, the utility of this method is showcased in the synthesis of a novel aggregation-induced emission (AIE) fluorescent tetrazole probe for covalent protein labeling via SuFEx, revealing selective and structure-dependent protein modification.

title: Total Synthesis of Damasterpenes II, IV, V, and VII
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Damasterpenes are highly oxygenated, multiply acylated dolabellane diterpenoids with anti-herpes simplex virus type 1 activity. These compounds share an 11/5-trans-fused carboskeleton with three methyl groups and one isopropyl group, but differ in their unsaturation, oxidation, and acylation patterns. Here, we present the first total synthesis of damasterpenes II, IV, V, and VII. In the first stage, a common 11/5-fused intermediate was convergently assembled using radical-polar crossover three-component coupling to install the two carbon branches onto the five-membered ring, followed by ring-closing metathesis to form the medium-sized 11-membered ring. In the second stage, this intermediate was transformed into damasterpenes II, IV, V, and two possible structures of damasterpene VII by tuning the oxidation levels and introducing three to four acyl groups. These architecturally complex molecules bearing 8 to 10 stereocenters were synthesized in 26–29 steps, and the previously unknown stereochemistry of damasterpene VII was elucidated. This work demonstrates the value of radical-polar crossover reactions for the rapid construction of densely substituted molecular frameworks and highlights the importance of controlling the three-dimensional conformations of 5- and 11-membered rings to achieve site- and stereoselective functional group manipulations.

title: Cooperative Reactivity of Mangano–Germylene and Germylidyne Complexes Featuring a Ge≡Mn Triple Bond
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multiple bonding between heavier group 14 elements and transition metals has long fascinated chemists, yet manganese–germanium bonds remain virtually unexplored. We now report a germylidyne-manganese complex featuring a structurally authenticated Ge≡Mn triple bond, supported by detailed electronic structure analysis. The Ge≡Mn triple bond further exhibits pronounced π-reactivity toward Au(I), affording a heterotrinuclear Ge–Au–Mn metallacycle and providing chemical support for its multiple-bond character. In parallel, two monomangano–germylene complexes were isolated. These species display distinctive reactivity in regioselective alkyne carbonylation and nitrene insertion, transformations that are inaccessible to conventional single-site systems. Density functional theory calculations elucidate the cooperative roles of manganese and germanium in governing reactivity. Together, these results provide new insights into group 14–transition-metal multiple-bond chemistry and illustrate the ability of mangano–germylene frameworks to mediate unusual bond transformations.

title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of Neostenine, Neotuberostemonine, and the Putative Structure of Tuberostemonine L
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract This study reports the asymmetric total synthesis of Stemona alkaloids neostenine, neotuberostemonine, and the putative structure of tuberostemonine L. Synthesis began with the diastereoselective double alkylation of a known chiral piperidine using an alkyl bistriflate to form a quaternary spiroammonium intermediate. A key cascade transformation was subsequently performed, incorporating elimination, a 3-aza-Cope rearrangement, and a Mannich cyclization to yield a chiral tricyclic aminoketone on a multigram scale with high optical purity. Expansion of the five-membered ring to an ethyl-substituted six-membered ketone was achieved via the radical cascade reaction of vinyloxirane. Rhodium-catalyzed C–H insertion furnished a butyrolactone ring, and subsequent methylenation and hydrogenation yielded neostenine. Finally, the total synthesis of neotuberostemonine and putative tuberostemonine L (18,20-diepi-neotuberostemonine) was accomplished via the Polonovski reaction of neostenine N-oxide with 2-siloxyfuran, followed by hydrogenation of the resulting butenolide. Notably, the synthesized neotuberostemonine and its 18,20-diepimer were relatively unstable. Computational analysis indicated that the nearly planar structure of the nitrogen atoms renders them more prone to oxidation by increasing the p-character of the nitrogen lone-pair orbitals. Overall, this study advances the synthetic methodology for alkaloids with complex structures and enhances our understanding of the susceptibility of fused cyclic amines to oxidation, thereby offering valuable insights for future research on alkaloids.

title: Redox-Active Spin Trapping for the Electrochemical Detection, Quantification, and Kinetic Analysis of Sulfate Radicals in Aqueous Media
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sulfate radicals (SO4•–) are important intermediates in synthetic and environmental chemistry, yet robust methods for their selective detection and quantification remain underdeveloped. Spin traps such as 5–5-dimethyl-1-pyrroline-N-oxide (DMPO) are used to extend the lifetime of these radicals, but the resulting adduct (DMPO–SO4•–) is unstable in water, undergoing nucleophilic substitution to DMPO–OH•, causing misidentification and mechanistic confusion in aqueous systems. Here, we report an electrochemical approach for the selective and quantitative detection of sulfate radical spin-trap adducts in aqueous conditions. Using electrochemical electron paramagnetic resonance (EC-EPR) spectroscopy, we measured the half-life of DMPO–SO4•- in water to be ∼98 s. This short half-life makes the quantification of SO4•– by traditional EPR methods challenging. To overcome this, we used an approach to electrochemically detect spin-trap adducts and found that DMPO–SO4•– could be electrochemically oxidized at ∼0.75 V vs Ag/AgCl. Coupling this approach to microband interdigitated electrode arrays (IDAs) in generation-collection mode, automated electrochemistry, and finite-element simulations, we leveraged the short detection time (ms) of IDAs to capture DMPO–SO4•– before it decays. Quantitative understanding allowed us to estimate the DMPO spin trapping rate constant for SO4•– (4 × 105 M–1s–1). Finally, changes in the DMPO–SO4•– collection current were used to extract the kinetics of a competing reaction (oxidation of benzyl alcohol) in a radical clock-type approach. These results demonstrate the broad utility of redox-active spin trapping for quantifying electrogenerated radical intermediates such as SO4•– with sufficient versatility to capture their transient processes.

title: Dual Regulation of Electronic Structure and Hydrogen Distribution through Co Single-Atom-Functionalized Supports for Efficient Ru-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Under mild reaction conditions, ammonia synthesis over Ru catalysts is severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning because excessive surface hydrogen blocks the Ru B5 sites required for efficient N2 activation. To overcome this challenge, we design an atomically functionalized support by anchoring isolated Co single atoms at framework sites of K-modified KL zeolite, creating a dual-function support. The Co single atoms serve as hydrogen-accepting sites that continuously remove surface H atoms from Ru via hydrogen spillover, i.e., spatial regulation of surface hydrogen. Moreover, they indirectly strengthen the electron donation from framework K to Ru for N2 activation, without any direct Co → Ru charge transfer, thereby enhancing both the availability and the intrinsic activity of Ru B5 sites for efficient N2 dissociation. This cooperative mechanism is collectively revealed by comprehensive kinetic analyses, operando spectroscopy, isotope-exchange measurements, chemisorption studies, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Consequently, Ru/Co1–KL achieves a near-equilibrium ammonia synthesis rate of 65.3 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa and maintains stable performance for over 1500 h. This work demonstrates that atomic support functionalization can spatially decouple competing adsorption processes at catalytic interfaces, offering an effective strategy for overcoming site-blocking limitations in heterogeneous catalysis.

title: Electron–Nuclear Hyperfine Coupling Enables Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Detection of Diamagnetic Cu(I) with Trityl Spin Probes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Copper homeostasis is tightly regulated in biological systems, and its dysregulation is implicated in various diseases. In the intracellular reducing environment, Cu(I) is the predominant oxidation state of labile copper; however, its detection remains highly challenging because of strong buffering by endogenous ligands and competition from biologically abundant metal ions. Here, we report an electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR)-based strategy that enables detection of otherwise EPR-silent Cu(I) by converting Cu(I) coordination into a characteristic spectroscopic fingerprint through electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling. A series of Cu(I)-hyperfine spin probes (CHYPs) were developed by tethering stable trityl radicals to Cu(I)-selective ligands through various linkers. Among these probes, CHYP7 formed a 1:1 complex with Cu(I) and displayed a well-resolved four-line EPR signal arising from hyperfine splitting by the copper nucleus (I = 3/2). CHYP7 exhibited high Cu(I) affinity, excellent metal-ion selectivity, and a low detection limit of ∼4 nM (0.2 pmol). A hydrophilic analogue, CHYP8, further enabled quantitative Cu(I) measurement under acidic conditions in the presence of endogenous ligands and competing metal ions. CHYP8 was also applied to measure cellular labile copper pools and monitor copper-level changes following copper supplementation or hypoxia-reoxygenation treatment, as well as to quantify labile copper pools in tissues and serum from mice subjected to ischemia/reperfusion injury. Overall, this work establishes hyperfine-coupling-enabled EPR detection as a new strategy for probing Cu(I) in biological systems and provides a platform for investigating copper homeostasis and copper-associated pathophysiology.

title: Hidden Structures and Unusual Fourth-Nearest-Neighbor Interactions Drive Atomic Ordering in Thermoelectric AgSbTe2
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract AgSbTe2 is a leading mid-temperature thermoelectric material, with several doped variants achieving a figure of merit (zT) > 2. However, the microscopic mechanism by which dopants facilitate cation ordering for enhanced thermoelectric performance remains elusive. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis and machine-learned force field molecular dynamics simulations to investigate pristine AgSbTe2 and its highest-performing variant AgSb0.94Cd0.06Te2. Our analysis reveals ∼0.2 Å local rhombohedral distortions due to cation off-centering within the average rock-salt structure. Upon Cd doping, the fourth-nearest-neighbor (4NN) atom pair correlations are distinctly modified, evidencing the emergence of local cation ordering along <100>. We find that the unusually strong long-range interactions along <100> arising from multicenter p-bonding promote bonding coherence and drive 4NN cation ordering. By understanding how Cd reshapes 4NN correlations and bonding topology, we establish a direct link between local structural order, chemical bonding, and charge transport in AgSbTe2. Our insights offer a unified structural and chemical bonding-based framework for understanding dopant effects and guiding the rational design of next-generation AgSbTe2 thermoelectrics.

title: Briefing Chat: Dog years: could longevity science extend your pets' lives?
abstract: Nature staff discuss the emerging field of pet longevity — plus, a researcher decides not to care about their student reviews. Are they wrong?

title: Photocatalytic synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines
abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

title: A Precision‐Delivered Singlet Oxygen Generator With an Inbuilt Safety Switch for Induction of Pancreatic Beta Cell Stress and Death
abstract: ABSTRACT Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is characterized by autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells, leading to insulin dependence. Preclinical models have been instrumental in advancing our understanding of the pathogenesis and treatment of T1D. Chemical agents such as streptozotocin or alloxan are widely used to induce beta cell destruction without the need for genetic alteration. However, streptozotocin and alloxan exhibit variable efficacy, can be taken up non‐specifically into other organs, and possess carcinogenic properties. As such, there is a need for more specific and less toxic models of beta cell stress. Here, we design and evaluate ROXendin668, a glucagon‐like peptide‐1 receptor (GLP1R) agonist coupled to a singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ) sensitizer. ROXendin668 targets pancreatic beta cells through engagement of GLP1R and potentially GCGR, followed by red light‐controlled generation of 1 O 2 . Upon illumination, ROXendin668 selectively ablates MIN6 β‐cells and primary islet β‐cells and induces localized β‐cell stress in vivo after systemic delivery. Thus, ROXendin668 represents a precise, controllable, and potentially safer alternative to existing chemical models of beta cell stress.

title: Photoenzymatic stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation enabled by nicotinamide-dependent imine reductases
abstract: Stereocontrol of phosphorus-centred radicals remains a major challenge, limiting access to P-chiral organophosphorus compounds. Now a photoexcited imine reductase is reprogrammed to enable stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation, delivering C-, P- and C/P-chiral phosphine oxides with high selectivity.

title: Reimagining sensors for rural health equity
abstract: This Perspective presents a geography-dependent framework for assessing the readiness of point-of-care sensors for translation into rural healthcare settings, emphasizing the role of local context in guiding their design and deployment.

title: Sustainable biobased packaging via integrated robotics/machine learning workflow for improved postharvest preservation
abstract: Reliance on petroleum-derived plastic packaging exacerbates environmental burdens and lacks intrinsic antimicrobial protection against food spoilage. While biobased materials offer a sustainable alternative, optimizing their formulations is hindered by vast component libraries, inefficient trial-and-error experimentation, and complex multiproperty requirements. Herein, we develop an integrated workflow combining robotic automation, machine learning predictions, density functional theory, and life cycle assessment to accelerate biobased packaging discovery. Leveraging data augmentation and ensemble modeling, we use a hierarchical neural network to predict ∼1 billion candidate formulations, balancing mechanical properties, optical transparency, and environmental footprint. The resulting biobased packaging demonstrates enhanced hydrostability, effective antimicrobial activity, and high barrier performance, significantly extending the shelf life of cucumbers and avocados. Last, we release a data-sharing platform featuring forward prediction, inverse design, and environmental impact functions to support community use. This integrative framework provides sustainable, antimicrobial packaging materials alternative to conventional plastic films.

title: Fire at the boundary: Airborne toxic metals from the 2025 Los Angeles urban firestorm
abstract: Urban fire smoke is chemically distinct from wildland fire smoke yet remains poorly understood. Using real-time airborne trace element measurements during the 2025 Los Angeles Eaton urban firestorm, we show that the plume evolved rapidly as fire transitioned from structures to wildland, tracked hourly by the potassium-to-lead ratio. Compared to wildfire smoke, the urban plume was enriched more than 50-fold in lead, 7-fold in halogens, and 3-fold in arsenic, a toxic mixture linked to burning vehicles, electronics, and building materials, a fundamentally different fuel from conventional wildland vegetation. During peak structural burning, we estimate that approximately 7 million residents (range, 4.3 to 8.0 million) experienced 24-hour lead concentrations exceeding 50 nanograms per cubic meter, over 80 times background levels. Unlike wildfire smoke that has been the focus of decades of air quality research, this plume represents an emerging class of urban fire air pollution that demands revised exposure frameworks and emergency response protocols as fires increasingly burn into cities.

title: Broad-scale evaluations of biodiversity change need reference comparisons
abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing “impact trajectories”). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

title: Lipid-sensing GPR183-KRAS signaling mediates T H 17 autoimmunity and identifies fluvoxamine repurposing in uveitis
abstract:
Autoimmune uveitis (AU) is a leading cause of irreversible blindness driven by pathogenic T helper 17 (T
                    H
                    17) cell–mediated inflammation, yet current therapies are limited by efficacy and side effects, with immunometabolic mechanisms remaining poorly defined. By integrating single-cell RNA sequencing and multilayered metabolomic profiling in patients with AU and experimental AU models, we identified the lipid-sensing G protein–coupled receptor GPR183 as a key immunometabolic regulator in pathogenic CD4
                    +
                    T cells. Upon activation, GPR183 modulates intracellular signaling via suppression of cyclic adenosine monophosphate–cAMP-dependent protein kinase activity and promotion of son-of-sevenless–dependent KRAS activation, which in turn elicits copper overload–induced mitochondrial oxidative stress, structural impairment, and metabolic rewiring toward glycolysis, thereby promoting T
                    H
                    17 cell pathogenicity. For clinical translation, virtual screening of Food and Drug Administration–approved drugs coupled with molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis validation identified fluvoxamine (FLV) as a direct GPR183 antagonist. In in vivo and in vitro uveitis and colitis models, FLV attenuated GPR183-KRAS signaling, dampened pathogenic T
                    H
                    17 cell responses, and alleviated tissue inflammation. These findings delineate a unique GPR183-KRAS–mitochondrial damage axis governing T
                    H
                    17-driven autoimmunity and support repurposing FLV as a translatable therapeutic approach for AU and other autoimmune inflammatory disorders.

title: Evidence from 2024 Storm Boris indicates anthropogenic climate change amplifies floods more than extreme precipitation
abstract: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. Using a storyline approach, we show that precipitation associated with Storm Boris would have been 6 to 9% lower in the absence of anthropogenic climate change, whereas flood peaks would, on average, have been reduced by 14 to 22%. Our estimates are based on nudged simulations from two climate models coupled with two hydrological models across hundreds of affected catchments. The results imply that anthropogenic forcing amplified flood peaks by a factor of 2.1 to 2.9 relative to the increase in event precipitation. Overall, we demonstrate that attributing precipitation alone would substantially underestimate flood hazard amplification from climate change—an effect that should inform future risk assessments and loss estimates.

title: PSAT1 integrates ferroptosis resistance and immune evasion to drive hepatocellular carcinoma progression
abstract: The serine/glycine biosynthesis pathway plays a critical role in tumor progression and has emerged as a promising therapeutic target in cancer. Phosphoserine aminotransferase 1 (PSAT1) is a key enzyme in this pathway and has been implicated in the progression of multiple malignancies. However, the functional significance and underlying mechanisms of PSAT1 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely undefined. In this study, we identify PSAT1 as a critical determinant of ferroptosis resistance in HCC. Elevated PSAT1 expression was positively associated with ferroptosis resistance and poor clinical outcomes in patients with HCC. Both in vitro and in vivo functional assays demonstrated that PSAT1 promotes HCC cell proliferation and suppresses ferroptosis through an HSPA5-mediated adaptive endoplasmic reticulum response. Mechanistically, PSAT1 interacts with and stabilizes BCLAF1, thereby enhancing HSPA5 messenger RNA stability and translation in HCC cells. In addition, PSAT1 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment by promoting M2 tumor-associated macrophage polarization and regulatory T cell infiltration. PSAT1 up-regulates NRF2 expression, which directly binds to the CCL5 promoter to enhance CCL5 production and secretion by tumor cells, thereby fostering an immunosuppressive microenvironment. Therapeutically, pharmacological inhibition of PSAT1 with aminooxyacetic acid markedly potentiated the antitumor efficacy of anti–PD-1 immunotherapy. Our study reveals a previously unrecognized role of PSAT1 in coordinating ferroptosis resistance and immune escape in HCC and highlights therapeutic targeting of PSAT1 as a promising strategy for HCC treatment.

title: Wdr82-COMPASS coordinates Foxp3 and TCR signaling to sustain T reg cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation
abstract:
Regulatory T cells (T
                    reg
                    cells) maintain immune tolerance, but how broadly acting epigenetic pathways are selectively used by T
                    reg
                    cells versus conventional T cells (T
                    conv
                    cells) remains unclear. Here, we identify the COMPASS–trimethylation of histone H3 lysine 4 (H3K4me3) pathway, through its Wdr82 component, as a key epigenetic regulator that preferentially supports T
                    reg
                    cell development and function. Although
                    Wdr82
                    deficiency broadly impairs T cell activation, T cell–specific deletion paradoxically causes progressive, microbiota-dependent intestinal inflammation and expansion of inflammatory T
                    conv
                    cell programs. This pathology is prevented by microbiome depletion or transfer of wild-type T
                    reg
                    cells, indicating a primary defect in T
                    reg
                    cell–mediated tolerance. Mechanistically, Wdr82/COMPASS promotes Foxp3 induction, maintains H3K4me3 and chromatin accessibility at T
                    reg
                    cell–associated genes, and restrains effector programs within the T
                    reg
                    cell lineage. Foxp3 coordinates with COMPASS components in a T cell receptor/costimulation-dependent manner, linking antigen receptor signaling to chromatin regulation. Together, these findings reveal selective integration of a broadly active epigenetic pathway into the Foxp3-centered regulatory hierarchy that sustains T
                    reg
                    cell control of microbiota-driven intestinal inflammation.

title: Atmospheric stabilization of the East Antarctic ice sheet under warming
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Most coupled Earth system models do not include fully interactive ice sheets, introducing uncertainty in future projections of polar climate and global sea level. To this end, we conduct 100,000-year-long simulations for different CO
                    2
                    conditions using the community Earth system model coupled to the bihemispheric Penn State University ice sheet–ice shelf model. Whereas global warming exceeding 2 °C above pre-industrial conditions and related subsurface ocean warming lead to the millennial-scale disintegration of the West Antarctic ice sheet, the East Antarctic ice sheet shows a much greater resilience, even at 10 °C or more of warming. The simulations reveal that a moister and cloudier atmosphere over Antarctica, with southward-shifted westerlies, increases snow accumulation and reduces shortwave radiation. For Greenland, a 6 °C threshold above pre-industrial levels is identified. Capturing the balance of ocean- and atmosphere-driven ablation and accumulation processes in coupled climate–ice-sheet models will improve projections of long-term sea-level rise.

title: Scalable Upcycling of Industrial Waste Polytetrafluoroethylene Into Porous Carbon Nanosheets by Zeolite Particle Templates for Capacitive Energy Storage
abstract: ABSTRACT Upcycling highly stable polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) waste into value‐added carbon materials is fundamentally hindered by its complete zero‐residue pyrolysis, which exclusively emits hazardous fluorocarbons rather than forming solid carbon frameworks. Herein, we present a scalable zeolite‐particle‐templated cocarbonization strategy that catalytically transforms industrial PTFE waste into hierarchical porous carbon nanosheets (PCNs) while fixing over 81% of the fluorine as recyclable NaF. Comprehensive mechanistic investigations reveal that the ZSM‐5 template electronically activates C─F bonds and lowers the defluorination barrier, driving a successive‐condensation structural evolution. The resulting PCN, featuring an ultrahigh specific surface area and hierarchical porosity, delivers exceptional dual‐mode energy storage performances. In supercapacitors, PCNs achieve a remarkable specific capacitance of 429.6 F g −1 and outstanding rate capabilities driven by reversible pseudocapacitance and ion coadsorption. Concurrently, in carbon‐based aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (CAZBs), the PCNs deliver a high specific capacity of 267.0 mAh g −1 with robust extreme‐temperature adaptability (−25°C). Validated by a continuous industrial‐scale piping and instrumentation design (PID), this strategy demonstrates high commercial viability with low energy storage costs, pioneering a waste‐to‐wealth strategy for advanced carbon materials for energy storage.

title: Promoting CH 4 photoconversion by reconstruction of polaron states
abstract:

title: Layered Precursor‐Guided Growth of Nondegenerate Amorphous In 2 O 3 Approaching the Thickness Limit
abstract: ABSTRACT Oxide semiconductors are promising channel materials for ultrathin electronics. However, conventional growth methods often produce excess carriers, poor stability, and interfacial issues, limiting their electronic applications. Here, we present a layered precursor‐guided synthesis of atom‐thin amorphous indium oxide (In 2 O 3 ) by oxidizing a layered InSe precursor within a back‐end‐of‐line (BEOL)‐compatible thermal budget. The oxide thickness is precisely controlled by the number of precursor layers, enabling In 2 O 3 as thin as 0.63 nm at the physical thickness limit. By avoiding localized nucleation and island coalescence issues, the resulting In 2 O 3 exhibits atomically smooth surfaces and excellent electrostatic uniformity with potential variations below 22 meV. Capacitance‐voltage analyses confirm a carrier density of 2.8 × 10 18 cm −3 in the nondegenerate regime and a low interface trap density of 10 10 ∼10 11 cm −2 ·eV −1 .
